If you have no church, find a faithful one near you and go this Sunday. Look for one where Christ is preached from the whole Bible, where baptism and the Lord’s Supper are given as he commanded, and where elders watch over the flock. Then ask how to join it. Christ never meant for one of his sheep to walk alone. If you do not know where to start, write to me . I keep this site. I am not a pastor, and I cannot always answer quickly. In an emergency, do not wait on me. Call 911 , or call 988 or text 988 . But I will pray for you, and I will help you look for a church. Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort; Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God. 2 Corinthians 1:3-4 (KJV) One day you may sit with someone else in this same dark. The comfort God gives you now is meant to be passed on.

title: Grief and Hard Times
text: If you do not know him Do You Believe This? Maybe you came here because of a death, a diagnosis, a broken home, or a lost job, and you are not a Christian. The promises here belong to those who belong to Christ. They can be yours. Jesus spoke these words to a grieving woman on the road outside her village, four days after her brother was buried ( John 11:17 , 20). Then he asked her a question. He asks you the same one. Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this? John 11:25-26 (KJV) If you came here grieving someone, this is not a word about them. Leave them with God. It is a word about you. Death came into the world through sin, and one day you will stand before God yourself ( Romans 5:12 , Hebrews 9:27 ). But Christ died in the place of sinners and bore the punishment their sins deserved, and on the third day he rose again. Everyone who turns from sin and trusts him alone is forgiven and counted righteous for his sake (Shorter Catechism Q&A 33, 87). He said that whoever comes to him he will in no wise cast out ( John 6:37 ). Call on him tonight, in your own words. Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved ( Romans 10:13 ). Do not wait until the grief lifts. Come as you are, with the grief. The gospel page sets it out in full. Read it slowly.

title: When Someone You Love Has Died
text: The house is quiet, or it is full of people, and either way the one you want is not in it. You do not have to be strong tonight. Christ has stood where you are standing.

title: When Someone You Love Has Died
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Not tonight. This isn’t a search for some sin behind their death. God hasn’t told you why, and no one may guess ( Deuteronomy 29:29 ). Your grief isn’t sin. Jesus wept. Grief may also expose bitterness, envy, or anger. Bring those things before the Lord as you notice them. Pray, Search me, O God, and know my heart ( Psalm 139:23 ). You may pour out all your sorrow to God, and even ask him why. Jesus did, on the cross. But don’t accuse him. Job lost his children in one day, and in all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly ( Job 1:22 ). Watch for bitterness toward family or friends ( Ephesians 4:31 ). Watch for drink or drugs to dull the nights. Don’t stay away from worship for long. And don’t let love for the one you lost take the place of God. Loving them isn’t the sin. Living for them in place of him would be. If you find any of this in you, don’t despair. Thomas wasn’t with the others the first time the risen Jesus came. Eight days later he was back with them, and Jesus came again and said, Peace be unto you ( John 20:24-26 ). Christ died for sins like these, and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes to him. Confess it, and he is faithful and just to forgive ( 1 John 1:9 ). If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Someone You Love Has Died
text: Through the Next Few Days Eat and sleep. Grief wears out the body. Eat something at each meal, even a little, and go to bed at your usual time. If you can’t eat or sleep for days, see your doctor. Say yes to one offer of help. When someone asks what they can do, give them a real answer. Let one person bring a meal or run one errand. Read Psalm 23 once a day. Read it slowly and pray it back to God. If one verse is all you can take in, that’s enough. Don’t make big decisions yet. Don’t sell the house, move, or give away their things this week. Those choices can wait. Ask someone you trust before you sign anything. Handle one practical task. Pick one thing, like one phone call or one form. Do just that one, and let the rest wait for another day.

title: When Your Husband or Wife Has Died
text: The one who knew you best is gone, and half of every habit in the house went with them. There is no timetable for this. Christ saw to those left behind even while he was dying.

title: When Your Husband or Wife Has Died
section: When you're ready to ask about heaven
text: When you're ready to ask about heaven If your husband or wife belonged to Christ, their soul is with him now, made perfect in holiness (Shorter Catechism Q&A 37). At the resurrection, believers being raised up in glory, shall be openly acknowledged and acquitted in the day of judgment, and made perfectly blessed in the full enjoying of God to all eternity. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q&A 38 Paul says that when the Lord comes, the dead in Christ shall rise first. Then his people who are still alive will be caught up together with them, and so shall we ever be with the Lord ( 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17 ). In the resurrection, Jesus said, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven ( Matthew 22:30 ). Yet Christ’s people are raised as themselves, with bodies made like his glorious body ( Philippians 3:21 ). Marriage is God’s gift for this life ( Romans 7:2 ). Scripture says less than we might wish about how his people will know one another there. But the one who gave his mother a home from the cross is there now, and he is their joy. If you’re his, you’ll see him on the day he chooses, not the day you choose. Until then, he hasn’t finished with your life here.

title: When Your Husband or Wife Has Died
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Your grief isn’t sin. Missing them isn’t sin, however long it lasts. This isn’t a search for some sin behind their death. God hasn’t told you why, and no one may guess ( Deuteronomy 29:29 ). But a long sorrow opens doors. Ask God to search you ( Psalm 139:23 ). Naomi buried her husband and both her sons. She said, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara ( Ruth 1:20 ). Mara means bitter. You may tell God it’s bitter. Don’t let it take root against him or his people. Loneliness can keep you home from worship. It can send you to drink to fill the evenings. It can rush you toward someone new before you've grieved and sought counsel. And the one you lost can come to fill the place only God should fill. God didn’t scold Naomi, and he didn’t leave her alone. From her house came King David, and at last Christ ( Ruth 4:14-17 , Matthew 1:5-6 ). He hasn’t promised you her ending. He offers you her Redeemer. Like Anna, keep close to God’s house and to prayer ( Luke 2:37 ). If you find any of this in you, bring it to Christ. He died for sins like these and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes to him. Confess it, and he is faithful and just to forgive ( 1 John 1:9 ). If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Your Husband or Wife Has Died
text: Facing the Empty House Keep your hours. Go to bed and get up at your usual times. Keep simple food in the house, and sit down to eat it, even alone. Don’t make big decisions yet. Don’t sell the house, move, or give away their things this week. Those can wait. Ask an elder or a trusted friend before you sign anything. Handle one practical task. Pick one thing, like calling the bank or finding the papers you need. Ask a friend to sit with you while you do it. Let the rest wait. Read Lamentations 3 in the morning. Read verses 21 to 24 when you first wake. Write one verse on a card and keep it by the bed. Go to church Sunday. Sit with someone you know. If walking in alone is too hard, ask a friend to pick you up.

title: When Your Child Has Died
text: No parent should outlive a child, and every part of you knows it. Whether you lost a baby you barely held, or never held at all, or a son or daughter you raised, Christ has not looked away.

title: When Your Child Has Died
section: If you lost a baby or a little child
text: If you lost a baby or a little child People brought young children to Jesus, some of them infants ( Luke 18:15 ). When his disciples rebuked those who brought them, Jesus was much displeased, and said, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not ( Mark 10:13-14 ). Suffer here means allow. And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them. Mark 10:16 (KJV) That's his heart toward little ones. Those hands were later nailed to a cross for sinners, and on the third day he rose ( John 20:25 ). His heart hasn’t changed. David said to God, Thou hast covered me in my mother’s womb ( Psalm 139:13 ). Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them. Psalm 139:16 (KJV) Unperfect means not yet fully formed. David was speaking of life in the womb. God saw your child before your child was fully made. The psalm speaks of God's complete knowledge of your child before birth. However early the loss came, you lost a child. When King David’s baby son died, David rose from the ground and worshipped ( 2 Samuel 12:20 ). Then he told his servants why. And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether God will be gracious to me, that the child may live? But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me. 2 Samuel 12:22-23 (KJV) David stopped fasting because the time for asking was over. The time for grief wasn’t over. He spoke of his son with hope, and then he went on living. He ate that same day, and he comforted his wife ( 2 Samuel 12:20 , 24). You may weep for your little one. Earlier in that chapter the prophet Nathan told David that this child would die because of David’s sin. In the same breath he told him, The Lord also hath put away thy sin ( 2 Samuel 12:13-14 ). No prophet has told you that your child died for your sin, and God hasn’t said it. Without a word from God, no one may trace a sorrow to a particular sin ( John 9:3 , Deuteronomy 29:29 ). Many mothers blame their own bodies. A body that couldn’t carry a child isn’t a sin. If you’re in Christ, there’s no condemnation for you ( Romans 8:1 ), and your baby’s death isn’t a sentence on you. For a believer even a Father’s chastening is never payment for sin, because Christ paid it all. A little one can’t understand a sermon or put faith into words. That’s no barrier to the Spirit of Christ, who works when, and where, and how he pleases ( Westminster Confession 10.3 ). Grace doesn’t wait for anyone to be old enough. The Canons of Dort, a sister Reformed confession, teach that believing parents need not doubt the salvation of the children God takes in infancy. They rest this on God’s Word, which calls the children of believers holy ( 1 Corinthians 7:14 ), not by nature but by his covenant of grace (Canons of Dort 1.17). That hope rests on God’s promise, not on how well you lived. Whatever you don’t know tonight, you may leave your child with the Judge of all the earth, who will do right ( Genesis 18:25 ). If your baby died before birth, the next part is for you. If not, go on to the part for every grieving parent .

title: When Your Child Has Died
section: If your baby died before birth
text: If your baby died before birth A miscarriage or a stillbirth is the death of a child. Some people around you may not see it that way. They may say nothing at all. Or they may say it was for the best, or that you can try again. They usually mean well, but a child isn’t replaced by another child. Scripture counts the little one you carried as a person, known by God and made in his image ( Jeremiah 1:5 , Luke 1:41 ). You aren’t making too much of this. You lost a son or a daughter. Many mothers search their memories for what they did wrong. Doctors find that most early losses come from causes no mother could have caused or stopped. And even where you wonder, God hasn’t laid this at your feet. He knoweth our frame ( Psalm 103:14 ). Fathers grieve this too, though often more quietly and later. A father may feel he has to be strong for his wife and so never mourn at all. Husbands, weep with your wives, and let your church care for you both. If the loss came early, there may be nothing to bury, and no one outside your home may have known. That can make the grief lonelier. You may still mark it. Give your baby a name, tell your pastor, and pray together as a family. Due dates and the day of the loss may be hard for years, and that isn’t a weakness of faith. If you’re afraid to hope for another child, or if another child never comes, bring that fear to the God who gives and takes away ( Job 1:21 ). He isn’t cruel, and he isn’t careless with you. If in the past you chose to end a pregnancy, you may grieve that child too. A doctor’s care after your baby had already died isn’t that choice. For that choice there's full pardon in Christ, for all who come to him. Read If You Have Had an Abortion and What I did is too great to forgive . The next part is for parents of an older child. The part for every grieving parent is for you too.

title: When Your Child Has Died
section: If your son or daughter was older
text: If your son or daughter was older Jesus once met a funeral at the gate of a town called Nain. The dead man was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow ( Luke 7:12 ). And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not. And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise. And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother. Luke 7:13-15 (KJV) A bier was the open frame the dead were carried on. Jesus had compassion on her before she asked him for anything. He could tell her not to weep, because he was about to give her son back. He wasn’t rebuking her tears, or yours. He didn’t raise every dead son or daughter in Israel. The widow’s son at Nain, and the girl of twelve he took by the hand ( Mark 5:41-42 ), were signs. They pointed ahead to the last day, when he will call his people out of their graves. They weren’t promises for today. When a great wind brought a house down on Job’s children, Job tore his robe, fell down on the ground, and worshipped. In all this Job sinned not ( Job 1:18-22 ). Grief and worship stand on the same ground. If your son or daughter trusted Christ, no man can pluck them out of his hand ( John 10:28-29 ). Death couldn’t do it either ( Romans 8:38-39 ). The souls of believers are at their death made perfect in holiness, and do immediately pass into glory; and their bodies, being still united to Christ, do rest in their graves till the resurrection. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q&A 37 If they're his, they’re with him now, and every sin they ever fought is gone. If you don’t know where your child stood with God, that’s too heavy to carry alone tonight. You aren’t asked to settle where they are. Leave them with the Judge of all the earth, who will do right ( Genesis 18:25 ), and bring your own soul to Christ. Read When You Fear They Did Not Know Christ , and tell your pastor this week. If your son or daughter took their own life, that sorrow has its own place here . If someone else took your child’s life, by carelessness or by violence, your anger at that wrong isn’t sin in itself. Scripture says, Be ye angry, and sin not ( Ephesians 4:26 ). God says, Vengeance is mine, and he promises to repay ( Romans 12:19 ). He gave the ruler the sword for this very wrong ( Romans 13:4 ), so pressing for justice in the courts isn’t revenge.

title: When Your Child Has Died
text: For every grieving parent Many parents replay every moment, what they ate or lifted, the last night, the keys they handed over, the sign they missed. Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him. For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust. Psalm 103:13-14 (KJV) You couldn’t see what only God could see. Moses told God’s people that underneath are the everlasting arms ( Deuteronomy 33:27 ). Those arms are a picture, since God is a Spirit, and the care they picture is real. But the Son of God took a real body, with real arms. He took up little children in those arms and blessed them. Then he died for sinners, and on the third day he rose. Now he says he was dead and is alive for evermore, and holds the keys of death ( Revelation 1:18 ). Keys picture his authority over death, and that authority is real. He will lose none of those the Father has given him, and he will raise them up at the last day ( John 6:39 ). Before you sleep, do these three things. If your child died long ago and the grief hasn’t let go, that isn’t a failure of faith. These are for you too. Pour out your heart to God. He is a refuge for us ( Psalm 62:8 ). Tell him all of it tonight. You don’t need fine words. Call your pastor or an elder. Even at night. Let him help you with a burial or a service if you want one, even for a baby lost early. You may give your baby a name. If you have no church, call a Christian friend, and read Do Not Carry It Alone below. Eat a little, and rest. Lie down even if sleep won’t come. If you’re married, be patient with each other. Husbands and wives grieve differently, and fathers often grieve later and more quietly. If you have other children, keep them close. They grieve too. If your body is healing from this loss, rest, and call your doctor if the bleeding is heavy or you have a fever. If you find yourself wanting to follow your child, call 988 or text 988 tonight, and tell someone near you.

title: When Your Child Has Died
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Not tonight. This isn’t the replaying of every moment, and it isn’t a search for some sin behind your child’s death. God hasn’t told you why, and no one may guess ( Deuteronomy 29:29 ). Your grief isn’t sin. But this sorrow can open doors. Ask God to search you ( Psalm 139:23 ). Anger at God may come. Tell him, but don’t charge him with wrong. Job lost all his children, and he did not charge God foolishly ( Job 1:22 ). Grief can turn a husband and wife against each other. Each may blame the other or shut the other out. If anyone at home hurt your child or is hurting you, get safe first . Otherwise, turn toward each other, forgiving one another ( Ephesians 4:32 ). Other people’s children may be painful to see. That ache isn’t sin, but it can grow into envy and bitterness. If you have other children, sorrow can make it hard to give them what they need. Let others help you care for them. If a heaviness won’t lift, that may be an illness and not a sin. See a doctor, and read When You Are Depressed . If you find any of this in you, don’t despair. Christ died for sins like these, and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes to him. Confess it, and he is faithful and just to forgive ( 1 John 1:9 ). If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Your Child Has Died
text: Help in the First Days Say yes to meals and rides. When someone offers, let them. Ask one friend to pass on the news for you, so you don’t have to tell it again and again. Leave the room as it is for now. You don’t have to pack anything away this week. Don’t make big decisions yet, like moving or giving things away. Those can wait. Handle one practical task. Pick one call or one form, and do just that one. Ask someone to sit with you while you do it. Let the rest wait. Read Psalm 103 together. If you’re married, read it aloud to each other one evening. Stop at verses 13 and 14, and pray them back to God. Look after your body. If your doctor asked to see you again, keep that visit. If you can’t eat or sleep for days, tell your doctor that too.

title: When You Fear They Did Not Know Christ
text: Some of us bury people we love without knowing whether they knew Christ. Some of you are not unsure. You fear you know. This is for you too, and you are not asked to settle anything tonight.

title: When You Fear They Did Not Know Christ
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Paul says, Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith ( 2 Corinthians 13:5 ). Don’t look for the answer in how strong your faith feels. Look to Christ. If you’re his and this fear has shaken you, read Am I Really Saved? This fear brings temptations of its own. One is to turn from God for their sake, as if staying away from Christ could help the one you lost. It can’t, and coming to him doesn’t betray them. Another is to think the Judge is hard. He is the one who wept over Jerusalem. Another is to keep accusing yourself for what you didn’t say. Bring that to Christ too. In him, whatever was truly sin is forgiven, and whatever was never in your hands you may lay down. Christ died on the cross for sinners and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes. Scripture still says, whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely ( Revelation 22:17 ). Come, and keep to the means he gave, his Word, prayer, and the Lord’s Day with his people.

title: When You Fear They Did Not Know Christ
section: Living With What You Can't Know
text: Living With What You Can't Know Eat and sleep. A heavy question wears out the body. Eat something at each meal, even a little, and go to bed at your usual time. Write the question down, then put it away. When the fear about where they are comes back, write it on paper and pray it to God once. Then put the paper away. Leave what you cannot know with the Lord. Pray for grace to live faithfully with the loss. Read Psalm 23 once a day. Read it slowly and pray it back to God, for yourself and for the ones still living. Say yes to help. Let one person bring a meal or sit with you for an evening. A grief with a hard question in it is still grief. Go to church Sunday. Hear the Word and pray with God’s people, even if you feel nothing. Sit with someone who knows what happened.

title: When Someone You Love Took Their Own Life
text: A death like this leaves questions no other death leaves. You may be carrying grief and guilt and fear all at once. God saw what you could not see, and he is near you now.

title: When Someone You Love Took Their Own Life
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Not tonight. In the weeks ahead, ask God to search you ( Psalm 139:23 ). Ask him to sort what’s truly yours from what isn’t. Much of what you carry may be false guilt. You didn’t choose this for them. If you truly sinned against them, confess it plainly, and in Christ it is forgiven ( 1 John 1:9 ). Even then, the choice wasn’t yours. What was never yours, you may lay down. Anger may come too, at the one who died, or at people you think should have seen it. Be ye angry, and sin not ( Ephesians 4:26 ). Don’t let it settle into bitterness. If it rises against God, tell him so, but don’t let it harden into a charge that he has done wrong. Shame may tell you to stay away from church. Go anyway. This death isn’t your disgrace. If the thought of following them comes, stop the searching and get help tonight. You're not strange, and you mustn't carry it alone. Call 988 or text 988 , and tell someone near you. Christ died on the cross for sinners and rose again. Whoever you are, come to him with what is truly yours, and leave the rest with him. If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Someone You Love Took Their Own Life
text: When the Grief Is Acute Save 988 in your phone. Do it today, so it’s there when you need it. If the thought of following them comes, call 988 or text 988 right away, and tell someone near you. Eat and sleep. Shock wears the body down. Eat something at each meal, even a little, and lie down at your usual time. Let someone help with the hard calls. There may be phone calls and papers you dread. Ask a friend or an elder to make them with you, or for you. Read Psalm 139 slowly. Read the first twelve verses once a day. Then tell God the one what if that weighs most on you today, and leave it with him. Go to church Sunday. Shame may tell you to stay home. Go, and sit with someone who knows what happened.

title: When Serious Illness Comes
text: One conversation in a small room, and the future looks different than it did this morning, for you or for someone you love. Or it has looked this way for years. You do not have to be brave tonight. Your times are in God’s hand.

title: When Serious Illness Comes
section: When it has gone on for years
text: When it has gone on for years You've asked for healing more times than you can count, and fewer people ask how you are. God put this prayer in the Bible for you. How long wilt thou forget me, O Lord ? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart daily? how long shall mine enemy be exalted over me? Psalm 13:1-2 (KJV) David felt forgotten, and he said so. A hidden face is a picture of a season when God’s favor can’t be felt, and such seasons are real ( WCF 18.4 ). But God hadn’t forgotten David, and by the end of the psalm David trusts his mercy again (13:5). For you it may take longer than six verses. He got there by praying the question, not by hiding it. If you’re his, the grace Paul was given is yours too. It doesn’t always take the weakness away. It holds you up inside it. Your outward man, the body, may be wasting away. Yet the inward man is renewed day by day ( 2 Corinthians 4:16 ). Paul also says the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us ( Romans 8:18 ). That doesn’t make your pain small. It makes the glory great. You may keep asking, and you may rest from asking. Let others pray when you can’t. And tell your elders you’re still here, since churches forget the long sick. If the long years bring thoughts of ending your life, tell someone near you, and call 988 or text 988 . God hasn’t finished with your life.

title: When Serious Illness Comes
text: If you're caring for someone Maybe it’s a hospital room, or hospice, or the long decline of a parent, a husband or wife, or a child. You're tired in ways few people see. When Lazarus was sick, his sisters sent Jesus this word, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick ( John 11:3 ). Pray that with their name in it. God told his people, even to hoar hairs will I carry you ( Isaiah 46:4 ). Hoar hairs are gray hairs. The carrying is a picture of his keeping, and his keeping is real. If they're his, he will carry them all the way, and if you're his, he carries you too. Caring for them is Christlike work. While he was dying, Jesus saw to his mother’s care ( John 19:26-27 ). Accept help, and give people real jobs, for we are told to bear one another’s burdens ( Galatians 6:2 ). Choosing a care home isn’t a failure of love. God works through means, and good nurses are among them. If dementia is taking their memory, they may no longer know your name. That’s a real grief, a goodbye that comes a little at a time, and you may mourn it. They may forget the Lord’s name too. If they are his, he won’t forget them ( Isaiah 49:15 ). Will God Keep Me to the End? says more.

title: When Serious Illness Comes
text: If death is near For those who belong to Christ, death doesn’t take them from him. It brings them to him. Jesus told the dying thief beside him, who had asked only to be remembered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise ( Luke 23:42-43 ). At death the souls of believers are made perfect in holiness and immediately pass into glory, and their bodies, still united to Christ, rest in their graves till the resurrection (Shorter Catechism Q&A 37). Christ rose, and they'll rise. Paul called being with Christ far better, yet said his staying was more needful for others ( Philippians 1:23-24 ). While God keeps you here, your days aren’t wasted. Jesus told his disciples not to let their hearts be troubled. He has gone to prepare a place for his people, and when he comes again he will receive them to himself, that where he is, they may be also ( John 14:1-3 ). You may face hard choices about treatment, for yourself or for someone who can no longer speak. The Larger Catechism forbids the neglecting or withdrawing the lawful and necessary means of preservation of life (Q&A 136). A treatment that can no longer preserve life, and would only lengthen dying, isn't such a means. You may say no to it, or stop it, and that isn’t giving up on God. But no one may end the life God gave, by a prescription or in any other way. Talk these choices over with your elders and your doctors. If you fear pain, ask about hospice care, which is there to ease it. If you fear being a burden, let those who love you carry you. If pain or fear is pushing you toward ending your life, tell someone near you, and call 988 or text 988 . Tell your family where your hope is, and call for your elders to pray with you ( James 5:14 ). If you dread dying itself, read Afraid of Dying . If you’re keeping watch at the bed, you don’t need many words. Hold their hand, read Psalm 23 aloud, and pray. If you don’t know where they stand with God, it’s not too late to pray for them, to speak of Christ simply, or to ask your pastor to come.

title: When Serious Illness Comes
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart This isn’t a search for why you’re sick. When his disciples asked whose sin had made a man blind, Jesus turned them from that question to the works of God ( John 9:2-3 ). It’s a look at how you’re bearing it. You may lament. David said, I poured out my complaint before him ( Psalm 142:2 ). Lament takes the complaint to God. Murmuring turns it against him, as if he had wronged you. The Larger Catechism counts patient bearing of the hand of God among the duties of the sixth commandment (Q&A 135). There's a quieter sin too, trusting the doctors and forgetting the Lord. Go to the doctor, and pray, My help cometh from the Lord , which made heaven and earth ( Psalm 121:2 ). Long pain can make us sharp with the ones who care for us. A caregiver may find resentment growing in the long nights. Needing care isn’t the sin, and it doesn’t make you a burden they would be better without. If you find these in you, bring them to Christ. He never murmured against his Father, and he went to the cross for murmuring sinners. He rose, and he turns away no one who comes. Confess it, and he is faithful and just to forgive ( 1 John 1:9 ). Then ask him for grace for this one day. If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Serious Illness Comes
text: Facing the Next Appointment Make the next appointment. If the next test or visit isn’t on the calendar yet, call this week. Bring your written questions and someone to listen with you. Take your medicine as prescribed. Use a pill box or a phone alarm if it helps. If something isn’t working or the side effects are hard, tell your doctor instead of quietly stopping. Pray Psalm 31:14-15 each morning. Say it out loud. Then put that day’s worries, by name, into his hand. Say yes to one offer of help. Let someone drive you, bring a meal, or sit with the one you’re caring for so you can sleep. Get to church if you can. If you can’t, ask your elders to visit you. Being sick doesn’t cut you off from God’s people.

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
text: You were left, or betrayed, or handed papers you did not want. The one who promised to stay did not. Whether you are the husband or the wife, Christ knows what it is to be betrayed.

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
section: What God has said about divorce
text: What God has said about divorce If you’re afraid at home, getting safe comes first , and all of this can wait. Leaving to be safe isn’t divorce, and it needs none of the grounds below. Someone may have told you that God hates divorce, as if it were a word against you. In Malachi God says he hateth putting away, and in the same breath he condemns violence. He was rebuking husbands who dealt treacherously against the wife of their youth ( Malachi 2:14-16 ). It’s a word against the one who breaks faith, not the one who was put away or left. Jesus named one ground for divorce, fornication ( Matthew 19:9 ). Paul speaks of a believer whose unbelieving spouse departs, and says God hath called us to peace ( 1 Corinthians 7:15 ). The Confession names only two grounds for divorce. One is adultery. The other is willful desertion that neither the church nor the government can remedy ( WCF 24.5 , 24.6). It protects the innocent party. It calls for a public and orderly course, so no one judges his own case. That’s a mercy. You don’t have to decide this alone, and this page won’t decide it for you. Your elders can guide you. If a door is still open and it’s safe, pray for repentance. With your elders’ help, seek reconciliation, as much as lieth in you ( Romans 12:18 ). If no one is hurting you, but you’re worn out and want out, that weariness is real. Tell God all of it. Then go to your elders before you take any step toward divorce ( 1 Corinthians 7:10-11 ). The heart is quick to find reasons, without just cause, to put asunder what God has joined ( Matthew 19:6 , WCF 24.6 ).

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Not tonight. This isn’t a search for your share of the blame. Adultery and desertion are the sin of the one who does them. Violence is never the fault of the one who is hurt. But any heart can sin in how it bears a wrong, and it’s a mercy to see it. Anger at a real wrong isn’t sin in itself ( Ephesians 4:26 ). But a wound can grow into bitterness, a grudge that grows out of sight. Paul says to put away all bitterness, and to be tenderhearted, forgiving one another ( Ephesians 4:31-32 ). Forgiving doesn’t mean saying it was small. It doesn’t mean trusting someone who hasn’t proved safe, going back into danger, or giving up on justice. It means giving up revenge and leaving the debt with God. Loneliness can also look for comfort in another person, in pornography , or in drink . Don’t start a new relationship until your elders have helped you see whether you’re free to marry ( WCF 24.5-6 ). If you find any of this in you, bring it to Christ, who died for sins like these and rose again. He turns away no one who comes, and he is faithful and just to forgive ( 1 John 1:9 ). If you’re his, ask him for grace to forgive as you've been forgiven. If shame or grief brings thoughts of ending your life, call 988 or text 988 , and tell someone near you.

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
section: If you're the one who broke faith
text: If you're the one who broke faith After David took another man’s wife and had the man killed, he wrote this. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise. Psalm 51:17 (KJV) A contrite heart is a crushed one. When Nathan confronted him, David said, I've sinned against the Lord . And Nathan said, The Lord also hath put away thy sin ( 2 Samuel 12:13 ). Christ died for sins like yours, and rose again. Tonight, tell God all of it, as David did. If you turn from your sin to Christ and confess it, God’s pardon is full at once. It rests on Christ’s blood, not on how well you confess ( WCF 15.3 ). Your wife’s or husband’s trust is another matter. It comes back slowly, if at all, and it’s theirs to give. You can’t make them trust you, or make them stay. Never use God’s forgiveness as a lever. Let your pastor or elders help you confess to your spouse without excuse ( WCF 15.6 ). Bear the consequences. If your sin has made them afraid of you, give them the distance they ask for. There’s more on forsaking this sin and fighting it under I have been unfaithful . If the shame tells you your family would be better off without you, that’s a lie. Call 988 or text 988 tonight. And if this sin feels too great to forgive, read What I did is too great to forgive .

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
text: If it's your parents It isn’t your fault. Nothing you said or did caused this, and it isn’t your job to fix it. You may keep loving both of your parents. You never have to carry messages between them, or pick a side. Tell an adult you trust how you’re really doing. That could be a parent, a teacher, a school counselor, or your pastor. David once wrote, When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take me up ( Psalm 27:10 ). To take up is to take in, the way a family takes in a child who has nowhere else to go. David meant that even if his own parents failed him, God wouldn’t. If your parents’ divorce feels like that, and you trust him, this is God’s word to you. It isn’t a verdict on your parents. Jesus was left alone too. The night he was arrested, all his friends ran away. He died for sinners and rose again. He never leaves anyone who trusts him. You can tell him exactly how you feel tonight, even if you’re angry. If anyone at home is hurting you, get safe first . If you ever think of ending your life, call 988 or text 988 . If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Your Marriage Is Breaking
text: Find Counsel and Support Read all of Psalm 55 . Read it slowly. Notice that David tells God everything, then leaves his burden with him. Pray it back in your own words. Sit down with your pastor or an elder. Set a time this week. Tell them what happened, and let them help you think through what comes next. Go to church Sunday. Go even if you dread being seen alone. Sit with someone you trust if that helps. Keep the ordinary things going. Eat at regular times, go to bed at a set hour, and go to work if you can. If you can’t sleep or eat for days, see a doctor. Say yes to help. When someone offers a meal, a ride, or an hour with the children, say yes.

title: When Your Child Walks Away From the Lord
text: You taught them to pray, and now they want nothing to do with Christ. You cannot give anyone a new heart. Only God can, and he has done it for sons and daughters as far off as yours.

title: When Your Child Walks Away From the Lord
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Your grief for your child is love, not sin. This isn’t a hunt for a cause. Your child’s sin is their own. Long sorrow can bring despair and harden your heart toward the child you love. One is despair, as if your child were beyond God’s reach. It's good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord ( Lamentations 3:26 ). Another is a hard heart toward your child. That looks like the cold word, or the door shut in anger and not for safety. In Jesus’ story the elder brother was angry, and would not go in when his brother came home ( Luke 15:28 ). Pray that if your child comes home, you'll run like the father. Another is the opposite. You hand over money that feeds their sin, or make excuses for it, and call it love. Another is turning on your husband or wife, as if blame could bring your child home. Longing for your child’s return is right. But it can become the thing you live for, more than Christ himself. If you find any of these in you, bring it to Christ, who died for sins like these and rose again. He turns away no one who comes, and he is faithful and just to forgive ( 1 John 1:9 ). Then keep praying for your child by name. If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When Your Child Walks Away From the Lord
section: As You Pray for Your Child
text: As You Pray for Your Child Read all of Luke 15 . Read the lost sheep, the lost coin, and the lost son together. Notice who goes looking, and who rejoices. Set a daily time to pray for your child. Pick a time you can keep, and pray for them by name. Ask a friend from church to pray with you for the same thing. Send one kind word. If it’s safe, send a short note or message that says you love them. Don’t preach in it. Just keep the door open. Decide your limits ahead of time. Settle what you will and won’t do about money, rides, or a place to stay. If you’re married, decide it together. Ask an elder to help you think it through, then hold to it. Go to church Sunday. Go even if it hurts to see other families whole. You need the Word and the prayers of God’s people too.

title: When You Lose Your Job or Home
text: The job or the business is gone, or the savings, or a fire or a flood took the house. It is hard to be the one who is supposed to provide. If you are his, your Father knows what you need.

title: When You Lose Your Job or Home
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Hardship brings temptations of its own. Even when the loss wasn't caused by your sin, you still need the Lord's help to endure it faithfully. Fear can harden into distrust of God. You may envy those who kept what you lost. Asaph confessed, I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked ( Psalm 73:3 ). Want can tempt you to cut a corner, or to chase quick money. Agur asked God for neither poverty nor riches, because he knew want could tempt him to steal ( Proverbs 30:8-9 ). If an employer wronged you, seeking what you’re owed is right. But don’t let a grudge take root. Pride can refuse help, or refuse humbler work. Humble work is no fall. The Son of God worked with his hands as a carpenter ( Mark 6:3 ). The job may also have been where you kept your worth. If you’re his, your worth is kept in Christ, and no lost job can touch it. If you find any of this in you, bring it to Christ, who became poor for his people, died, and rose again. He turns away no one who comes, and he is faithful and just to forgive ( 1 John 1:9 ). Then ask for this day’s bread, and do the next thing. If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When You Lose Your Job or Home
section: Ask for Help With the Immediate Need
text: Ask for Help With the Immediate Need Meet with a deacon. Don’t wait until the money is gone. Tell the deacons plainly what you have and what you’ll need over the next month. Make a budget for this month. Write down what’s coming in and what has to go out. Put rent, food, utilities, and medicine first. Cut what can wait. Apply for the help you qualify for. If you lost your job, file for unemployment right away. If a fire or flood took your home, call your insurance company and ask what aid is open to you. Look for work every weekday. Set regular hours for it. Tell friends from church what kind of work you’re looking for, and take honest work while you look for better. Keep the Lord’s Day. Go to church Sunday, even if you feel ashamed. Rest from the search that day and pray Psalm 46 .

title: When You Are Lonely
text: The house is quiet, or the room is full and no one knows you. You may have been alone for years. Christ knew what it was to be left, and he has not left you.

title: When You Are Lonely
section: God Gives the Lonely a Family
text: God Gives the Lonely a Family God doesn’t leave his people alone with him and no one else. The same psalm that calls him a father of the fatherless says, God setteth the solitary in families ( Psalm 68:5-6 ). He does it through his church. Jesus said that whoever does the will of God is his brother, and sister, and mother ( Mark 3:35 ). To those who leave house and family for his sake he promised houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, now in this time, with persecutions ( Mark 10:29-30 ). Those are the people of God, and if you’re his, they’re given to you. Saints, by profession, are bound to maintain an holy fellowship and communion in the worship of God, and in performing such other spiritual services as tend to their mutual edification; as also in relieving each other in outward things, according to their several abilities and necessities. Westminster Confession of Faith 26.2 That bond is real before anyone feels it. A church won’t always notice you without being told, and some of that's their sin. But you belong to them, and they to you. You may tell your elders that you’re alone. That isn’t complaining. It lets the church obey.

title: When You Are Lonely
text: If You're Single If you long to be married, the longing isn’t sin. God himself said, It is not good that the man should be alone ( Genesis 2:18 ). But marriage is his gift to give, and he doesn’t give it to every one of his people in this life. Paul was unmarried, and he said that every man hath his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that ( 1 Corinthians 7:7 ). A single believer isn’t loved less by God than a married one. If you marry, marry only in the Lord ( 1 Corinthians 7:39 ). Loneliness is a poor counselor in that choice. Talk it over with your elders and with believers who know you.

title: When You Are Lonely
text: If You're Married and Alone You may share a house and a name with someone and still be alone. Your husband or wife may not believe, or may have grown cold. Or they may simply not speak of the things you most need to say. Peter wrote to wives whose husbands obey not the word ( 1 Peter 3:1 ), so God hasn't overlooked you. Tell your pastor. If you’re afraid at home, get safe first . If your marriage is breaking, that has its own page .

title: When You Are Lonely
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Not tonight. Loneliness itself isn’t sin. It’s an ache God made you able to feel, and Christ felt it. Loneliness can tempt you to seek comfort in ways that leave you more isolated. Ask God to search you ( Psalm 139:23 ). It can send you to a screen at night for company, or to pornography , or to drink . It can rush you toward someone who doesn’t love the Lord. It can harden into self-pity, or into bitterness against a church that didn’t notice you. It can even keep you home from worship, the very place God gathers his people together. Elijah once told God, I, even I only, am left ( 1 Kings 19:10 ). God answered that he had kept seven thousand in Israel who hadn't bowed the knee to Baal (19:18). Your loneliness may tell you that no one else is faithful, or that no one cares. It may be wrong. If you find any of this in you, bring it to Christ, who was forsaken for sinners and rose again. He turns away no one who comes, and he is faithful and just to forgive ( 1 John 1:9 ). Then go to his people again this Lord’s Day, and sit near someone. If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When You Are Lonely
text: Reach Out to Someone Pray Psalm 142 . Read the whole psalm aloud. It’s seven verses. Say the lonely parts to God as your own. Make one phone call. Call someone in your congregation. A conversation can help more than another evening of messages. Ask how they are, and tell them how you are. Tell an elder you’re alone. Ask whether there’s a family you could eat with, or a small group or Bible study you could join. Go to church Sunday and stay after. Don’t slip out at the end. Find one person, learn their name, and ask how you can pray for them. Get outside each day. Take a walk, run an errand in person, or sit where people are. Plain daylight and ordinary faces help more than you’d think.

title: When You Are Depressed
text: For weeks or years the heaviness has not lifted, or it keeps coming back. Sleep does not rest you, and the promises you once loved seem to belong to someone else. Christ has been in the dark before you.

title: When You Are Depressed
section: When you're ready to search your heart
text: When you're ready to search your heart Do this in a better hour, and not alone if you can help it. It isn’t a hunt for a sin behind the dark ( John 9:3 ). For you, the searching should be short and the looking to Christ long. Who is among you that feareth the Lord , that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the Lord , and stay upon his God. Isaiah 50:10 (KJV) To stay upon God is to lean your whole weight on him. Watch for just a few things. The dark may tempt you to give up the Word, prayer, and worship, because they feel empty. Keep to them, even briefly, and let others pray with you. It may tempt you to dull the pain with drink or drugs , or to hide how bad it is. If the dark tells you that God will never be kind to you again, it’s lying. If the dark tells you that others would be better off without you, that’s a lie too. If thoughts of ending your life come, stop the searching and get help now. Don't keep them secret. Call 988 or text 988 , and tell someone near you. Where you find sin, confess it simply. Christ died for sinners and rose again, and he turns away no one who comes. So look away from yourself to him. If you don’t know Christ, or aren’t sure you do, his own question is below .

title: When You Are Depressed
text: Find Help and Keep Going Make the doctor’s appointment. Call today, or ask someone to call with you. Tell the doctor how long this has lasted and how bad it gets. Keep a simple routine. Get up and go to bed at the same times. Eat three plain meals. Take a short walk in daylight, even ten minutes. Read Psalms 42 and 43 together. The same question runs through both. Read them slowly, and each day answer your soul as the psalm does, hope thou in God. Let someone check on you. Ask one person to call or stop by every day or two. Tell them the truth when they ask how you are. Go to church Sunday. Go even if you feel nothing and can only sit. Let God’s people sing and pray for you when you can’t.

title: If You Are Not Safe
text: Some hard hours are dangerous. If yours is, the first faithful thing to do is to get safe. Read the rest later.

title: If You Are Not Safe
section: If you're thinking of ending your life
text: If you're thinking of ending your life Don't wait for morning, and don't wait until you can explain it well. Call 988 or text 988 . Then tell someone safe near you tonight, a husband or wife, a parent, a friend, or your pastor. If the means to end your life are near you, give them to someone to keep tonight, or put them where you can’t reach them. Your life isn't yours to end. It belongs to the Lord who made you. If you’re Christ’s, it’s his twice over, for ye are bought with a price ( 1 Corinthians 6:20 ). He died and rose for you, and he hasn’t finished with your life. The Larger Catechism counts it a duty of the sixth commandment to preserve our own lives as well as the lives of others (Q&A 135). When Elijah asked God to take his life, God sent him sleep and bread, and then work to do ( 1 Kings 19 ). Asking for help isn’t weakness. It’s obedience.

title: If You Are Not Safe
text: If someone is hurting you For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper. He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy. He shall redeem their soul from deceit and violence: and precious shall their blood be in his sight. Psalm 72:12-14 (KJV) This is a psalm about the true King, and Christ is that King. He isn’t neutral about what’s being done to you. A husband or a wife or anyone in your home may hit you, threaten you, force you, or make you afraid for your life or your children. If so, you may leave to be safe, and you should. The Larger Catechism names just defense against violence, and protecting and defending the innocent, among the duties God requires (Q&A 135). Scripture says a prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself ( Proverbs 22:3 ). When Saul threw a javelin at David, David fled, and his wife let him down through a window ( 1 Samuel 19:10-12 ). Jesus told his disciples that when they were persecuted in one city, they should flee into another ( Matthew 10:23 ). Leaving to be safe isn’t a lack of faith, and it isn’t a sin. You’re not to blame for another person’s violence. Questions about the marriage itself can wait, and your elders can help you with them later. Calling the police isn’t revenge, and it isn’t a betrayal of the church. Scripture calls the ruler the minister of God, who bears the sword against those who do evil ( Romans 13:4 ). Tell your elders too, once you’re safe. If the one hurting you is an elder, or close to one, tell another pastor you trust. If anyone tells you to go back into danger, don't go back. Go to the police, and find a pastor who will stand with you. Christ is the Bridegroom who gave himself for his bride, and who nourishes and cherishes her ( Ephesians 5:25 , 29). What’s being done to you is the opposite of what he does. When a crowd at Nazareth tried to throw him off a cliff, he passed through the midst of them and went his way ( Luke 4:29-30 ). His hour hadn't yet come. When it came, he gave himself up on the cross, of his own will and in the place of sinners. On the third day he rose. That work is finished. Your suffering can’t add to it, so you’re not called to stay under violence.

title: If You Are Not Safe
section: If a child is being hurt
text: If a child is being hurt If a child is in danger, call 911 now. Otherwise report it to the police or to your county’s child protective services. Childhelp can tell you how. Don't wait for anyone at church to handle it first. Abuse is a crime, and God gave the civil ruler the sword to punish it. A faithful church will stand with you when you call. If you’re young and someone is hurting you, tell a teacher or a school counselor today. If you’re in danger right now, call 911 . You can call Childhelp at 1-800-422-4453 at any hour. They’re trained for this, and the law requires them to act.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: For anyone worn down by a sin that will not let go. A heart gives up an old love only for a stronger one, and Christ is the one love strong enough to drive the others out.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: Read this first If You're Tired of Losing You may have fought this sin for years. You may be ashamed to make God the same promise one more time. This page is for you, and it doesn’t begin with a new promise. If your sin is hurting another person, especially a child, it stops now. Read My sin is hurting someone else before anything else. In danger, or thinking of ending your life? Call 911 , or call 988 or text 988 , now, and tell someone near you. If someone is hurting you, read If You Are Not Safe . Outside the United States, call your local emergency number. If you write to me about your sin, know first that I can’t keep a secret that leaves someone in danger. If your sin is hurting a child or anyone else, go to your pastor and the authorities before you write to me. Most of us tell God we’re done with a sin, and for a while the promise holds. Then a bad night comes, and the old sin walks back in as if it still had a key. A sin keeps its hold because the heart still loves it. So this page begins with what you love, and with the King you’re coming to, who will not break a bruised reed ( Isaiah 42:3 ). If you’re not sure you’ve ever come to Christ, read Where to Start first. If you’re near despair, go straight to When You Feel Like Giving Up . If there’s a sin you love and mean to keep, there’s an honest word for you too. If you use Mortify and temptation is on you now, open it and press Flee. Come back here later. If what troubles you is a thought you hate and never chose, read Doubts and Unwanted Thoughts first, since a page like this can feed that fear. For you, the searching should be short and the looking to Christ long.

title: Struggling With Sin
section: Why Promises to Stop Don't Last
text: The root Why Promises to Stop Don't Last Sin breaks God’s law, and at its root it’s love turned from God to something else. That’s why a promise to stop so seldom holds. The Westminster Shorter Catechism, part of the standard this site holds , begins with what you were made for. Man’s chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him for ever. Westminster Shorter Catechism Q&A 1 Your heart was built to want, and it never stops. The wanting is God’s gift, and sin has bent it. God named what we do instead through Jeremiah. For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water. Jeremiah 2:13 (KJV) A cistern was a pit cut in rock to catch the rain, and a broken one leaks. The sin you keep going back to is a cistern you dug. It promised rest after a hard day, or the feeling of being wanted, and it never held. Paul calls covetousness idolatry, love given to something that should never have had it ( Colossians 3:5 ). Thomas Chalmers, a Scottish minister, preached on this two hundred years ago in a sermon, The Expulsive Power of a New Affection. An affection is what the heart loves, and expulsive means driving out. The heart must have something to cling to, he said, and the only way to dispossess it of an old affection is by the expulsive power of a new one. Jesus told of a house swept clean and left empty, and of what came back to fill it ( Matthew 12:43-45 ). Nobody blows out his candle because someone proves it’s small. He sets it down when the sun is up. Chalmers didn’t mean that any new interest will do. The love that drives out the love of the world, he said, comes only when a man sees by faith God’s glory in the face of Jesus Christ. It comes when he hears Christ call all who will to a full pardon. Willpower can sweep the house. It can't fill it.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: A greater affection Look to Christ The one love strong enough to drive out the others is love for Christ, and it grows from seeing his love for sinners. God doesn’t ask you to work it up. He shows you his Son. But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord. 2 Corinthians 3:18 (KJV) A glass is a mirror, and the mirror is the gospel, which shows the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ ( 2 Corinthians 4:6 ). We slowly become like what we behold, and the Spirit does it. Paul says this of everyone whose heart has turned to the Lord (3:16). Beholding him doesn’t mean picturing his face (Larger Catechism Q&A 109). It means looking by faith at who Scripture shows him to be and what he does. Read the Gospels slowly. Watch him touch a leper ( Mark 1:41 ) and eat with sinners ( Luke 15:2 ). Sit under preaching that holds him out. If you’re a communing member of a faithful church, come to his Table. God grows a new love by these ordinary means. He offered living water to the woman at the well before she had changed anything, though her life was a row of broken cisterns ( John 4:13-18 ). He offers the same water to you. Where his pardon is known, love follows. Of the woman who wept at his feet he said, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven ( Luke 7:47 ). Her love was the fruit of that pardon, and it was her faith that saved her (7:50). We love him, because he first loved us ( 1 John 4:19 ). John Owen, an English Puritan pastor, gave the same counsel in his book Indwelling Sin, to fill your affections with the cross of Christ, that there may be no room for sin.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: If you're not his yet Where to Start Only those who belong to Christ can put sin to death. If you’re not his yet, your fight begins with him. Mortify means to put to death. Before giving any direction, Owen said that unless a man is truly joined to Christ, he can never mortify any one sin. Paul says that if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his ( Romans 8:9 ). So conversion comes first, and Owen said that’s no unkindness. If a man patches a hole in his wall while the house burns, the friend who points to the fire isn’t his enemy. Sin is a master, and only the Son can make you free indeed ( John 8:34-36 ). He lived the life you haven’t lived. He bore the curse in the place of all who trust him, and he rose again. He is freely offered to you, and he turns away no one who comes. If your sin is harming someone, stop today and get help ( My sin is hurting someone else ). Stopping is right, but it can’t make you his. The promises on this page belong to those who belong to Christ, and they can be yours. Come to Him tells you how.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: Mortification Putting Sin to Death Once the heart has seen Christ, it turns against the old love that still pulls at it. The Spirit gives it strength to put that sin to death. Paul joins what you love to what you do, and the hinge is one word. If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God. Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth. For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God. When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory. Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry: Colossians 3:1-5 (KJV) The therefore in verse 5 hangs on verses 1 to 4. If you’re his, you died with Christ and your life is hid with him in God. Only then does Paul say, Mortify. Inordinate affection is love out of order, and concupiscence is evil desire. The members to mortify are the sins in Paul’s list, not the limbs of the body. Jesus spoke the same way when he said to pluck out a right eye, or cut off a right hand, that offends, which means one that makes you stumble ( Matthew 5:29-30 ). He had just put lust in the heart (5:28), and a man with one eye can still lust. It’s a picture of cutting off whatever feeds the sin, even what you value most. God never asks you to harm your body (Larger Catechism Q&A 135-136). If you’re his, your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost ( 1 Corinthians 6:19 ). If you have hurt yourself, or feel driven to, call 988 or text 988 now. If you’re badly hurt, call 911 . In 1656 Owen built his book Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers on one verse. For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live. Romans 8:13 (KJV) Ye means believers, who are under no condemnation ( Romans 8:1 ). The flesh is the old sinful nature, not skin and bone. Ye do mortify means the work is yours, and through the Spirit means the strength is his. The if shows the path the believer walks. It doesn’t set a price on life, for Christ has already paid that for all who are his. Owen said that even the best believers must make this their business all their days. As he put it, be killing sin or it will be killing you. They who are once effectually called and regenerated, having a new heart and a new spirit created in them, are further sanctified, really and personally, through the virtue of Christ’s death and resurrection, by his Word and Spirit dwelling in them; the dominion of the whole body of sin is destroyed, and the several lusts thereof are more and more weakened and mortified, and they more and more quickened and strengthened, in all saving graces, to the practice of true holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord. Westminster Confession of Faith 13.1 Quickened means made alive, virtue means power, and a lust is any strong sinful desire. Saving graces are the holy habits the Spirit grows in God’s people, such as faith and humility. Notice the words more and more. The change is real and slow, and never finished in this life ( Westminster Confession 13.2 ). Owen warned that a calm temper, a hidden sin, or zeal after a scare kills nothing. The man who trades one sin for another hath changed his master, but is a servant still. The real thing is slower. Owen pictured a man nailed to a cross, who cries out loudly at first and more faintly as his blood drains away. He took the picture from Paul, who says, They that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts ( Galatians 5:24 ). Sin in a believer dies that way, and a new grace grows in its place. Owen also asked why you fight. True mortification, he said, rests on hating sin because it's sin, not only because it shames you, and on a sense of Christ’s love shown at the cross.

title: Struggling With Sin
section: Your Part and the Spirit’s Part
text: The daily work Your Part and the Spirit’s Part The Spirit doesn’t do this in your place, and you can’t do it without him. The Confession holds both together. Their ability to do good works is not at all of themselves, but wholly from the Spirit of Christ. And that they may be enabled thereunto, besides the graces they have already received, there is required an actual influence of the same Holy Spirit to work in them to will and to do of his good pleasure; yet are they not hereupon to grow negligent, as if they were not bound to perform any duty unless upon a special motion of the Spirit; but they ought to be diligent in stirring up the grace of God that is in them. Westminster Confession of Faith 16.3 A special motion means a special stirring. Some teach that a Christian should stop trying and let God do it, and the Confession won’t have it. Owen said of the Spirit that he works in us and with us, not against us or without us. God works in, so you work out ( Philippians 2:12-13 ), and work out never means work for. If you’re his, do these things, and begin each day with the first. Look to Christ before you look at the sin. Owen’s chief direction for killing sin was to set faith at work on Christ. He called Christ’s blood the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Come to the throne of grace for mercy for the last fall and grace for the next hour ( Hebrews 4:16 ). Strike at the first stirring. A man is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed, before the desire ever conceives and brings forth sin ( James 1:14-15 ). Strike before it conceives. Cut off what feeds it. Make not provision for the flesh ( Romans 13:14 ). With each sin God forbids all the causes, means, occasions, and appearances thereof (Larger Catechism Q&A 99). Put the phone out of the bedroom at night. Take a different road home. End the friendship that keeps leading you back. When you must, run. Joseph left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out ( Genesis 39:12 ). Bring it into the light. The Confession asks you to repent of your particular sins particularly (15.5). That means naming this sin to God plainly, and then being done. It doesn’t mean listing every passing thought. Then tell your elders, or a believer you trust of your own sex. Sin deceives, and God’s remedy is to exhort one another daily ( Hebrews 3:13 ). If you’re young, tell a parent, or another adult you trust, such as a teacher or your pastor. If you’re the pastor, tell an elder or a minister you trust. Keep to the means. Watch and pray ( Matthew 26:41 ). Put your baptism to use by drawing strength from the death and resurrection of Christ, into whom we are baptized, for the mortifying of sin (Larger Catechism Q&A 167). Sit under the Word in a church, and not only on a screen. If you’re a communing member, come to the Table ( Life After You Believe ).

title: Struggling With Sin
section: Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. Behold, we come unto thee; for thou art the LORD our God.
text: Mortify, a help for the daily work Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. Behold, we come unto thee; for thou art the LORD our God. Jeremiah 3:22 (KJV) I made a free app for the work this page describes. It goes where you go. Mortify Free · Works in any browser · Sign up to begin Open it on your phone and add it to your home screen. Then it opens like an app. Open Mortify See all it does When temptation comes, open it, press Flee, and choose the sin. It gives you Scripture for that sin, a word from a Puritan such as John Owen or Thomas Watson, a prayer, and something to do right now. It may tell you to put the phone in another room, or to go where people are. Each morning there’s a reading, and each night a few honest questions. After a fall it doesn’t scold you. It turns you back to Christ ( more on Mortify ). It’s a help, not a Savior. It can’t fight in your place or stand in for Christ, his Word, or your church.

title: Struggling With Sin
text: Particular sins Porn, Adultery, Anger, and Addiction Some sins bring danger with them, to you or to someone near you. They’re fought the same way, with your eyes on Christ, but they need more help than a page can give. If none of these is yours, go on to When You Feel Like Giving Up . Two things first. If you cut or starve or purge yourself, see a doctor this week. If you feel driven to hurt yourself, call 988 or text 988 now. And what was done to you by force, or by an adult when you were a child, isn’t your sin to put to death ( If You Are Not Safe ). I can't stop looking at what I shouldn't If these are thoughts you hate and never chose, this section isn’t for you. Go to Doubts and Unwanted Thoughts . If it’s pornography, name it to yourself and to God. Christ was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin ( Hebrews 4:15 ), and there's grace to help at his throne (4:16). Put the screen out of reach at the hours you fall, and tell someone. If you’re young, tell a parent, or if you can’t, another adult you trust. If you’re married, ask your pastor or an elder to help you bring it into the light at home. If you’re an adult and what you look at shows anyone under eighteen, a real child was abused to make it, and looking at it's a crime. Stop today, and read My sin is hurting someone else . If you’re young and an adult showed you these things or asked you for pictures, it’s being done to you. The same is true if anyone at any age threatens to share pictures of you. Don't pay, and don't send more. Stop answering, and don’t delete the messages. If you’re young, tell a parent or another adult you trust today. If you’re grown, tell the police. If it feels like more than you can live through, call 988 or text 988 . I've been unfaithful If it’s still going on, end it today, with no contact, as Joseph fled ( Genesis 39:12 ). If the affair was physical, see a doctor and be tested, for your spouse’s sake and your own. For confessing to your husband or wife, read If you are the one who broke faith . If you catch yourself thinking your family would be better off without you, that’s a lie. Call 988 or text 988 . My anger frightens my family A harsh husband or wife, father or mother, is the opposite of the gentle King. Tears after an outburst aren’t yet repentance. If you have hit, choked, forced, or threatened anyone at home, or broken things to frighten them, that's abuse and a crime. Give them the distance they ask for. Don't press them to forgive you, to take back what they told anyone, or to sit in counseling with you. Tell your elders, and accept that the police may be involved. If you’re afraid you'll hurt someone, leave the house and call 911 . Give any guns in the house to someone to keep. If you’re the one who is afraid, read If You Are Not Safe . Drink or drugs have hold of me Paul sets a better filling against drink, Be filled with the Spirit ( Ephesians 5:18 ). God works through means ( Westminster Confession 5.3 ), and a doctor and treatment are among them. If you drink heavily every day, or take a pill like Xanax or Valium every day, don't stop all at once on your own. That can bring seizures and can kill. See a doctor this week, tell the whole truth about how much you use, and let someone go with you. Tell your pastor or an elder too. After even a few days off opioids, your old dose can kill you. If someone has taken too much, call 911 , and give naloxone (Narcan) if you have it. Don’t stop a prescribed medicine without asking your doctor. My sin is hurting someone else If these are thoughts you hate and never chose, this section isn’t for you. Go to Doubts and Unwanted Thoughts . If you haven’t acted, but you fear a desire toward a child, don't be alone with children. Tell a doctor and your pastor this week. A doctor can tell a fear you hate from a desire you must fight, and there’s help for both. If you've harmed someone, the harm stops first. If it touches a child, stay away from children today, your own included. If the child lives with you, you’re the one who leaves the house, today. Don't ask the child or anyone in the family to keep it quiet. Tell your pastor, and know that harm to a child must be reported to the police or to child protective services. A faithful church won’t keep it secret. Accept what the law does ( Romans 13:4 ), for pardon with God doesn’t cancel earthly justice. Christ turns away no one who comes, and coming to him means coming into the light, for he that doeth truth cometh to the light ( John 3:21 ). This time is dangerous for your own life too. If you’re thinking of ending it, call 988 or text 988 now.

title: Struggling With Sin
section: When You Feel Like Giving Up
text: Assurance When You Feel Like Giving Up If you’re his, you don’t fight for your place with God. You fight from it. Justification is God’s verdict that pardons a sinner and counts him righteous for Christ’s sake. Sanctification is his lifelong work of making him holy. The Larger Catechism sets them side by side. Although sanctification be inseparably joined with justification, yet they differ, in that God in justification imputeth the righteousness of Christ; in sanctification his Spirit infuseth grace, and enableth to the exercise thereof; in the former, sin is pardoned; in the other, it is subdued: the one doth equally free all believers from the revenging wrath of God, and that perfectly in this life, that they never fall into condemnation; the other is neither equal in all, nor in this life perfect in any, but growing up to perfection. Westminster Larger Catechism Q&A 77 Imputeth means credits to your account, and infuseth means pours in. The pardon is the same in every believer and perfect today, whatever your week was like. The subduing of sin is uneven in all and finished in none. Your standing rests on the first, and the second is the evidence that you have it ( Justification by Faith Alone ). A boy who breaks a window is in trouble with his father, but he isn’t an orphan again. The Confession gives assurance three grounds. They're God’s promises, the graces he works in his children, and his Spirit’s witness ( Am I Really Saved? ). In Grace Abounding, John Bunyan tells how he saw that his good frame of heart didn't make his righteousness before God better, nor his bad frame make it worse. He wrote, my righteousness was Jesus Christ Himself. Some think fear keeps a struggling Christian careful. The Confession says otherwise. A true believer may wait long and fight hard before he has assurance, so lacking it doesn’t prove you aren’t his. Seek it all the same. The Confession calls that seeking a duty, and assurance makes a Christian stronger in the fight, never looser. This infallible assurance doth not so belong to the essence of faith, but that a true believer may wait long, and conflict with many difficulties before he be partaker of it: yet, being enabled by the Spirit to know the things which are freely given him of God, he may, without extraordinary revelation, in the right use of ordinary means, attain thereunto. And therefore it is the duty of every one to give all diligence to make his calling and election sure; that thereby his heart may be enlarged in peace and joy in the Holy Ghost, in love and thankfulness to God, and in strength and cheerfulness in the duties of obedience, the proper fruits of this assurance: so far is it from inclining men to looseness. Westminster Confession of Faith 18.3 Looseness means careless living. So Paul promises all who are under grace, For sin shall not have dominion over you, and he gives the reason, for ye are not under the law, but under grace ( Romans 6:14 ). A hired hand works in dread of losing his place. That slavish fear, as the Confession calls it (20.1), never taught a heart to love. A son works his father’s field because it’s his father’s. His fear is a son’s fear of grieving the father who loves him, and in that fear believers go on perfecting holiness ( 2 Corinthians 7:1 ). I fell again today Then go back to Christ tonight, sin and all. Micah spoke for God’s people when they were brought low for their sin. When I fall, I shall arise, he says, and in the next breath, I have sinned against him ( Micah 7:8-9 ). After Peter denied him, the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter ( Luke 22:61 ), and Peter wept and was restored. Judas was sorry too ( Matthew 27:3 ), but he carried his sorrow away from Christ, the sorrow of the world ( 2 Corinthians 7:10 ). Carry yours to him. One grave sin can shake your assurance for a while, yet the seed of God remains in his children ( Westminster Confession 18.4 , and see When God Feels Far ). Confess it, for he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins ( 1 John 1:9 ). If you fear he must be tired of forgiving you, read When the Same Sin Keeps Coming Back . If the shame tells you that you’d be better off dead, or that others would be better off without you, it’s lying. Call 988 or text 988 now, and tell someone near you. I don't feel that I love him You may not feel your love for him, yet long to be free of your sin and to love him more. Look at the longing itself. Owen said that longing, breathing, and panting after deliverance is a grace in itself. Peter wrote to believers, Whom having not seen, ye love ( 1 Peter 1:8 ). The Larger Catechism (Q&A 172) asks what you want, not whether you have won yet . You must truly be Christ’s to put sin to death, Owen said. But you needn’t first be sure that you are ( Westminster Confession 18.3 ). Your hope rests on Christ and his promise, not on how the fight is going. The fight itself is one of the marks of his Spirit in you. So look to Christ, and fight. Richard Sibbes wrote in The Bruised Reed that there's more mercy in Christ than sin in us.

title: Struggling With Sin
section: If You've Made Peace With It
text: An honest word If You've Made Peace With It This part isn’t for the one who hates his sin and keeps losing. It’s for the one who has stopped fighting and made a home for it. If you hate your sin, even as you fall, or if reading this makes you want to fight, it isn’t describing you. Go on to the last section . The first half of Romans 8:13 is a real warning to the church.
