Westminster Confession of Faith 1.9 Scripture interprets Scripture, so a hard place is read in the light of plainer ones. And the true sense of a passage is one, not many. There's a right reading, and it’s worth the work of finding. Take heart. Not everything in Scripture is equally plain. But what you must know, believe, and do to be saved is set out clearly. An ordinary reader, using ordinary means, can understand it ( WCF 1.7 ). A hard chapter in Daniel can’t take Christ from you.

title: How to Read the Bible Rightly
section: Know What Kind of Writing It Is
text: Know What Kind of Writing It Is God spoke at sundry times and in divers manners ( Hebrews 1:1 ). Each kind of writing is read by its own rules, and every one is wholly true. History tells what happened. Luke wrote that Theophilus might know the certainty of those things ( Luke 1:3-4 ). Law commands. Thou shalt not steal ( Exodus 20:15 ) means what it says. Israel’s ceremonial and civil laws have ended with Christ and that nation, but the moral law still binds ( WCF 19.3-5 ). Poetry sings in pictures. The Lord is my shepherd ( Psalm 23:1 ) is a figure, and the care it pictures is real. Proverb tells how God has ordered life to go as a rule. A soft answer turneth away wrath ( Proverbs 15:1 ), though not every angry man softens. See Is Proverbs 22:6 a Promise? Prophecy speaks for God, often in vivid pictures. Micah named Bethlehem as the Ruler’s birthplace centuries ahead ( Micah 5:2 ), and there Christ was born ( Matthew 2:5-6 ). The guide to reading prophecy says more. Parable is a story Jesus told to teach. In the sower, Jesus explains that the seed is the word of God ( Luke 8:11 ), and that lesson is true. Letter was written to a real church about real problems. Now concerning the things whereof ye wrote unto me ( 1 Corinthians 7:1 ). Ask what the apostle was answering, then hear it as written to you. Apocalyptic vision shows heavenly things in symbols. John hears of the Lion of the tribe of Juda, turns, and sees a Lamb as it had been slain ( Revelation 5:5-6 ). Both pictures show one real Christ, who conquered by dying.

title: How to Read the Bible Rightly
section: How to Tell a Figure of Speech
text: How to Tell a Figure of Speech When you’re unsure, ask these questions. Would the plain sense be absurd? Jesus said, I am the door ( John 10:9 ). He isn’t wood on hinges. He is the one way into God’s fold, and that’s no less true for being said in a picture. Would it contradict other Scripture? Under his wings shalt thou trust ( Psalm 91:4 ). But God is a Spirit ( John 4:24 ), without body or parts ( WCF 2.1 ). So the wings are a figure, and what they picture is real, his near and sheltering care. Does the Bible explain it? Jesus said, Destroy this temple, and John tells us he spake of the temple of his body ( John 2:19-21 ). Is it overstated on purpose? When Jesus says to pluck out the offending eye ( Matthew 5:29 ), he isn’t asking you to maim yourself, since sin comes from the heart ( Mark 7:21 ). He means deal with sin without mercy, because hell is real. When none of these applies, take the words at face value. A figure always points to something real. The Lamb was truly slain. A figure makes a real thing easier to see and harder to forget. The opposite error Some readers, once they learn that the Bible uses figures, begin to treat its history as myth. That doesn’t read the author’s sense. It overrules it, and Christ himself closes that door. He grounded marriage on what God did when he which made them at the beginning made them male and female ( Matthew 19:4-5 ). He compared his coming to the days of Noah, when the flood came, and took them all away ( Matthew 24:37-39 ). A pretend flood is no warning of a real judgment. He set his three days in the grave beside Jonah’s three days in the fish ( Matthew 12:40 ), and said the men of Nineveh will rise in the judgment ( Matthew 12:41 ). Paul sets Adam beside Christ, one real man beside another ( Romans 5:12-19 ). If Jesus read these chapters as history, his disciples may not do less. And the God who raised his Son from the dead isn’t strained by a great fish.

title: How to Read the Bible Rightly
section: Read for Christ, and With the Church
text: Read for Christ, and With the Church On the road to Emmaus the risen Lord taught his disciples to read their Bibles. Beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself ( Luke 24:27 ). Later he showed them that the law, the prophets, and the psalms were all written concerning him. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures ( Luke 24:44-45 ). Christ is the center of the whole Book. The Passover lamb whose bones were not broken ( Exodus 12:46 , John 19:36 ) and the servant wounded for our transgressions ( Isaiah 53:5 ) lead to him. If you finish a passage and haven’t seen your need of him, read it again. If you’ve never come to him, the gospel is where to start. Context and the church Read every verse in its paragraph and its book. Most errors start with a verse torn from its setting, the way the unlearned and unstable wrest the scriptures ( 2 Peter 3:16 ). And don’t read alone. How can I, except some man should guide me? the Ethiopian asked ( Acts 8:31 ). The Confession and Catechisms are the church’s careful summary of what Scripture teaches. They keep you from inventing a reading no faithful Christian has held. Trusted commentaries like Matthew Henry help too. Read the text first, then the help, and bring your questions to your pastor. Where faithful teachers differ On some questions godly, confessional men have differed. The Confession says God made all things of nothing, in the space of six days, and all very good ( WCF 4.1 ). The Reformed Presbyterian Testimony adds that Genesis 1 and 2 are history, not mythology, and that man didn't evolve from any lower form of life (RP Testimony 4.1, 4.4). Most have held the days to be ordinary days, while some confessional teachers have read their length another way. Faithful men differ too on the millennium of Revelation 20 (see The Thousand Years ). On questions like these, study, hold your view honestly, and hold it humbly. The secret things belong unto the Lord our God, but those things which are revealed belong unto us ( Deuteronomy 29:29 ).

title: How to Read the Bible Rightly
text: Steps for This Week Pray before you read. Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law ( Psalm 119:18 ). Name the kind of writing before you read each passage. Work through one hard passage. Read the whole chapter, ask the four questions above, and follow the cross references in your margin. Ask where Christ is. Write one sentence on how the passage points to him. Check yourself against the church. Read Matthew Henry on it, or find where the Confession speaks to it. Sojourner puts both beside the text. Obey what is plain. Don’t let a hard verse keep you from what a clear one commands today. For a plan to read the whole Bible, see How to Read the Bible .

title: How to Read Prophecy and Revelation
text: What all Reformed believers hold about the end, how prophecy works, how to read Revelation, and the thousand years.

title: How to Read Prophecy and Revelation
text: What Every Reformed Believer Holds Christians agree on more about the end than they think. Start with what’s settled. God hath appointed a day wherein he will judge the world in righteousness by Jesus Christ, to whom all power and judgment is given of the Father. Westminster Confession of Faith 33.1 Christ will come again visibly and bodily. This same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven ( Acts 1:11 ). He cometh with clouds, and every eye shall see him ( Revelation 1:7 ). The dead will rise together, the just and the unjust. All that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth ( John 5:28-29 ). Then comes the judgment, and after it two endings that never end, everlasting punishment for the wicked and life eternal for the righteous ( Matthew 25:46 ). And no one knows when. Of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only ( Matthew 24:36 ).

title: How to Read Prophecy and Revelation
text: How Prophecy Works Much of prophecy comes in pictures. Daniel saw four great beasts come up from the sea, and he was told they are four kings ( Daniel 7:3 , 17). John saw Christ as a Lamb as it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes ( Revelation 5:6 ). Christ isn’t an animal with horns, but he really was slain, and he really reigns. The sign points to a real work of God. Interpret it in the light of the passage and the rest of Scripture. Prophecy often has a nearer and a farther fulfillment. God promised David a son who would build a house for his name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever ( 2 Samuel 7:13 ). Solomon built the temple, but he died and his kingdom split. Hebrews gives the same promise to Christ ( Hebrews 1:5 ). The near son pointed to the far one. Above all, let the New Testament show you how the Old is fulfilled. At Pentecost Peter said, But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel ( Acts 2:16 ). Paul says the promises were made to Abraham and his seed, which is Christ ( Galatians 3:16 ). So when you read a prophecy, ask first how it points to him.

title: How to Read Prophecy and Revelation
text: How to Read Revelation Revelation was sent and signified by an angel to John ( Revelation 1:1 ). That means it was shown by signs. John wrote as your brother, and companion in tribulation, exiled on Patmos for the word of God ( Revelation 1:9 ). Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand. Revelation 1:3 (KJV) These visions were given to comfort a suffering church. Their message is plain even where the details are hard. The Lion of the tribe of Juda hath prevailed, and he is the Lamb that was slain ( Revelation 5:5-6 ). Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life ( Revelation 2:10 ). Read the numbers and beasts as signs. The book explains some of its own figures. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches ( Revelation 1:20 ). Like Daniel’s beasts, its beasts picture real powers that rage against Christ. They aren’t riddles to solve with this year’s politicians. Read it with the rest of Scripture. Its pictures come from Daniel, Ezekiel, and Zechariah. Hard places are explained by other places that speak more clearly ( WCF 1.9 ). Keep the main thing main. If you finish a chapter knowing more about a beast than about the Lamb, read it again.

title: How to Read Prophecy and Revelation
text: The Thousand Years Revelation 20:1-6 tells of Satan bound that he should deceive the nations no more, and of souls who lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. Reformed teachers who agree on everything above read this in two main ways. This page doesn’t choose between them. Amillennialism Amillennialists read the thousand years as the present age, between Christ’s first coming and his second. The number is a sign of a long and complete time, not a count of years. Satan was bound when Christ came, so the gospel now goes to the nations. Jesus asked, How can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? ( Matthew 12:29 ). The souls who reign are believers who have died and now live with Christ, waiting for the resurrection. On earth this view expects Christ to gather his people out of every nation while the age stays mixed. Wheat and tares grow together until the harvest ( Matthew 13:30 ). Geerhardus Vos and Louis Berkhof taught this view. Postmillennialism Postmillennialists believe the gospel will so prevail before Christ returns that the nations largely become Christian. Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance ( Psalm 2:8 ). Yea, all kings shall fall down before him, all nations shall serve him ( Psalm 72:11 ). The kingdom grows from a mustard seed into a tree, and works like leaven till the whole was leavened ( Matthew 13:31-33 ). The earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord , as the waters cover the sea ( Habakkuk 2:14 ). This comes by ordinary preaching and the Spirit’s power, and Christ returns at its close. Its teachers read the details of Revelation 20 in more than one way, but they share this hope. Jonathan Edwards, Charles Hodge, and B. B. Warfield held it. Both views hold that Christ reigns now, and he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet ( 1 Corinthians 15:25 ). Both expect one return, one resurrection, and one judgment. Both pray, Thy kingdom come. They differ on how much of the earth will bow before he comes, not on whether he is King. See also The Hope for the Nations . Premillennialism Many evangelicals are premillennial. They believe Christ returns before the thousand years and reigns on earth for those years. The righteous are raised at the start and the rest at the end. The view is old, and godly men have held it. Most Reformed teachers haven't, because Scripture speaks of one resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust ( Acts 24:15 ), with judgment following straight on Christ’s coming ( Matthew 25:31-32 ). Dispensational premillennialism goes further. It treats Israel and the church as two peoples with two plans, and it teaches a secret rapture years before Christ’s visible return. The Reformed reading finds neither in Scripture. Christ hath made both one ( Ephesians 2:14 ). And the catching up of the saints comes with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God ( 1 Thessalonians 4:16 ). That’s hardly secret. Many who hold these views love the Bible and long for Christ. Love them as brothers, but don’t mistake their charts for the Reformed faith. How It Ends says more.

title: How to Read Prophecy and Revelation
text: Don't Set Dates Men have named the year of Christ’s return again and again, and every one has been wrong. Of that day and hour knoweth no man ( Matthew 24:36 ). No preacher with a chart knows it either. Beware too of newspaper exegesis. That means reading the Bible through this week’s headlines. It shakes believers, which Paul warned against ( 2 Thessalonians 2:1-2 ). And it pulls your eyes off Christ and onto the news. Read the news in the light of Scripture, never the reverse. A teacher who sets dates has shown you not to follow him. See How to Spot a False Teacher .

title: How to Read Prophecy and Revelation
text: Watch and Be Ready As Christ would have us to be certainly persuaded that there shall be a day of judgment, both to deter all men from sin, and for the greater consolation of the godly in their adversity: so will he have that day unknown to men, that they may shake off all carnal security, and be always watchful, because they know not at what hour the Lord will come; and may be ever prepared to say, Come, Lord Jesus, come quickly. Amen. Westminster Confession of Faith 33.3 God hid the day to keep you awake, not to keep you guessing. Every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure ( 1 John 3:3 ). His coming is good news only for those found in him. If you’re not in Christ, the day you can’t know is the day to be ready for now. The gospel shows you how to come to him today. Read Revelation 1 to 5 and 19 to 22. Ask what each vision shows you about Christ. Learn Acts 1:11 by heart. Say it when the news frightens you. Pray Psalm 2 and Psalm 72 . Ask God to give his Son the nations, whatever you think about the thousand years. Ask if you’re ready. If Christ came tonight, is there a sin you would be ashamed to be found in? Put it away. See How to Examine Yourself . Turn off the prophecy charts. To go deeper, ask your elders for a sound book on the last things. Pray the Bible’s last prayer. Christ says, Surely I come quickly. Answer him every day, Even so, come, Lord Jesus ( Revelation 22:20 ).

title: How to Spot a False Teacher
text: Seven questions to test any teacher by Scripture, the common warning signs today, and what to do when you find one.

title: How to Spot a False Teacher
text: Christ Warned You Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Ye shall know them by their fruits. Matthew 7:15-16 (KJV) Jesus, Paul, Peter, John, and Jude all warned that false teachers would come from inside the church, not only from outside it ( Acts 20:29-30 , 2 Peter 2:1 , 1 John 2:19 , Jude 4). They rarely announce themselves. They're often likable, gifted, and popular. So Scripture tells you to test them, not to trust them because they’re famous or kind.

title: How to Spot a False Teacher
text: How to Test a Teacher Do what the Bereans did. They received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so ( Acts 17:11 ). Then ask these questions. What does he say about Christ? Is Jesus fully God and fully man, the only Savior, crucified for sinners and bodily raised? A man who teaches otherwise, and holds to it when he is shown the truth, isn’t a confused brother. He is a false teacher ( 1 John 4:1-3 , 2 John 9-10). Someone who was simply taught wrong and gladly takes correction is another case. Teach him patiently, as Aquila and Priscilla taught Apollos the way of God more perfectly ( Acts 18:26 ). What does he say about the gospel? Is a sinner saved by grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone? Anyone who adds works, rituals, or a church’s merit to Christ preaches another gospel ( Galatians 1:6-9 ). What is his final authority? Scripture alone, or Scripture plus his visions, his prophecies, or his church’s tradition? God has finished speaking in his written Word. Nothing is to be added to it by new revelations of the Spirit or traditions of men ( WCF 1.6 ). Does he handle the Bible honestly? Does he read verses in their setting, or pull them out to prove what he already wanted to say? The unlearned and unstable wrest the scriptures unto their own destruction ( 2 Peter 3:16 ). Does he call sinners to repent? A teacher who never names sin, never warns of judgment, and never calls for repentance isn’t preaching the gospel Christ preached ( Mark 1:15 , 2 Timothy 4:3-4 ). How does he live? Look at his fruit. Greed, sexual sin, pride, and love of money are marks Scripture names ( 2 Peter 2:2-3 , 10, 14, 18, Titus 1:11 ). Who holds him to account? Is he under the oversight of a church and its elders, or does he answer to no one?

title: How to Spot a False Teacher
text: Common Warning Signs Today Health and wealth. Teaching that God promises money, health, and success to those with enough faith, or to those who give to the ministry. New revelation. Claims that God told him something new that you must believe or obey. No sin, no judgment, no hell. A message only about self-esteem, purpose, and blessing. Christ made small. Jesus presented only as a good example, a life coach, or one way among many. Celebrity without a church. A large following, a brand, merchandise, and no elders. Anger at being tested. A faithful teacher welcomes being checked against Scripture. A false one calls it attacking God’s anointed.

title: How to Spot a False Teacher
text: Be Careful in Both Directions Not every teacher who is wrong about something is a false teacher. A sound minister can be mistaken on a lesser point, or say something badly. Faithful men have differed on baptism, church government, and the millennium. Some of those differences are serious errors, but they aren’t heresy. Save the label for those who deny or corrupt the gospel itself. How to Spot Real Heresy sets out the difference. Don’t become a man who hunts for heresy for sport. Test what you hear, hold fast that which is good ( 1 Thessalonians 5:21 ), and speak with grief, not glee. To see these questions put to work fairly on popular preachers of our day, read Teacher Reviews .

title: How to Spot a False Teacher
text: What to Do Stop following him. Unsubscribe, stop buying, stop giving. Paul says to mark them and avoid them ( Romans 16:17 ). Warn those you love, gently and with Scripture. If he is in your own church, go to your elders. Don’t start a campaign on your own. Sit under faithful preaching. The best protection from counterfeit is to know the real thing well. See How to Find a Faithful Church .

title: How to Spot Real Heresy
text: The difference between heresy, serious error, and honest disagreement, the truths that mark the line, and how to respond.

title: How to Spot Real Heresy
text: What Heresy Is Heresy denies truths essential to the Christian faith. A disagreement over a secondary doctrine doesn't by itself place someone outside the faith. Peter called them damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them ( 2 Peter 2:1 ). It helps to sort disagreements into three kinds. Heresy. Denies the gospel or the God of the gospel. Suppose a man holds it and still clings to it after patient teaching and a first and second admonition. He can’t be received as a brother in the faith, whatever he calls himself ( Titus 3:10 , 2 John 9-10). Serious error. Wrong on an important teaching, and harmful to the church, but not a denial of the gospel itself. Worth contending about. Not a reason to call someone lost. How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism shows where those two fall. Differences among the faithful. Questions on which godly, confessional Christians have disagreed for centuries, such as the millennium. Hold your view, and hold it charitably. Calling a teaching heresy is a judgment about the teaching, measured by Scripture. It doesn't give us knowledge of another person's heart. A man may be confused, badly taught, or not yet corrected, and God alone knows the heart ( 1 Samuel 16:7 ). But to reject an essential truth knowingly, and to go on rejecting it, is no small thing. Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ, hath not God (2 John 9). The church must judge what a man professes. The final judgment of every soul belongs to God ( Romans 14:10-12 ).

title: How to Spot Real Heresy
section: The Truths That Mark the Line
text: The Truths That Mark the Line The early church settled these in the Apostles’, Nicene, and Athanasian Creeds and at the Council of Chalcedon in 451. The Reformation recovered the gospel itself. Denying any of them is heresy. One God in three persons. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory ( WSC 6 ). Christ fully God. The eternal Son, not a created being or a lesser god ( John 1:1 , Colossians 2:9 ). Christ fully man. A true body and a reasonable soul, born of the virgin Mary ( WSC 22 , Hebrews 2:14-17 , 1 John 4:2-3 ). Christ one person. Two natures, not two persons, and not a mixture of the two ( WCF 8.2 ). His death for sinners and his bodily resurrection. If Christ be not raised, your faith is vain ( 1 Corinthians 15:17 ). Salvation by grace alone through faith alone. Any message that makes our works part of the ground of our acceptance with God is another gospel ( Galatians 1:6-9 , Romans 3:28 ). Scripture as God’s Word. A teaching that sets a new revelation or a church above Scripture cuts away the ground every other truth stands on.

title: How to Spot Real Heresy
text: Where It Shows Up Some groups that use Christian words deny these truths in their official teaching. Jehovah’s Witnesses deny the Trinity and teach that Jesus is a created being. The Latter-day Saints teach that God was once a man and that there are many gods, and they add books to Scripture. Oneness Pentecostals deny the Trinity and teach that the Father, Son, and Spirit are one person in different modes. The Roman Catholic Church teaches that justification is by God’s grace and that no one can earn the grace by which it begins. But it teaches that justification isn’t only the forgiveness of sins but the inward renewal of the sinner, given at baptism. It teaches that the righteousness by which a man is justified is the grace God pours into him. And it teaches that this righteousness is increased by good works done in grace. The Council of Trent, whose decrees Rome still holds, condemned anyone who says a sinner is justified by faith alone or by the imputed righteousness of Christ alone (Session 6, canons 9, 11, 24). Scripture teaches that God justifies the ungodly by counting Christ’s righteousness to him, received by faith alone ( Romans 4:5-6 , Philippians 3:9 ). To deny that is to deny the gospel the Reformers recovered ( WCF 11.1 ). The prosperity gospel teaches that Christ died to buy health and wealth for those with enough faith, and that faith is a force men use to get what they want. That makes gain the reward of godliness and turns the gospel of grace into another gospel ( 1 Timothy 6:5 , Galatians 1:6-9 ). This is about what each group officially teaches, not a verdict on every person in it. God alone knows each heart. People inside those groups need the gospel told to them plainly and kindly.

title: How to Spot Real Heresy
text: How to Respond Know the truth well. The surest guard is a firm grasp of the Shorter Catechism and the Creeds. See Reformed doctrine . Counterfeits are spotted by those who know the real thing. Earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints (Jude 3). Don’t shrug off heresy as a difference of opinion. Be gentle with the person. Paul says to instruct them in meekness, if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth ( 2 Timothy 2:25 ). Do not give a heretic a platform. John told the church not to receive one who brings another doctrine of Christ or to bid him God speed (2 John 10). Leave church discipline to the church. A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject ( Titus 3:10 ). That’s the elders’ work, not a private verdict.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: Who makes the difference when a sinner is saved? Both views set out fairly, answered from Scripture, and how to talk with a brother who disagrees.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: The One Question Underneath When a sinner is saved, who makes the difference between him and the man beside him who stays lost? Pelagianism and Arminianism answer differently, and neither gives the answer taught in the Westminster Confession. We need to understand the difference before we answer either one. These doctrines affect how we pray for conversion, preach the gospel, and seek assurance. They also answer who receives the credit for salvation. Paul put the whole question in one line. For who maketh thee to differ from another? and what hast thou that thou didst not receive? now if thou didst receive it, why dost thou glory, as if thou hadst not received it? 1 Corinthians 4:7 (KJV) Paul wrote those words to humble Corinthians who were puffed up over their favorite teachers ( 1 Corinthians 4:6 ). He wasn’t settling the debate this page is about. But the principle he lays down reaches further than Corinth. Whatever we have, we received. This page applies that principle to the greatest gift of all. Pelagianism denies the inherited corruption of Adam's descendants. Classical Arminianism acknowledges the fall and the need for grace, but holds that grace can be resisted and that faith isn't infallibly produced by effectual calling. Those errors are serious, yet they aren't the same error. This page tests both views against Scripture and the original Westminster Standards. Then it turns to practice. How to talk with a brother who disagrees. What not to overcorrect into. Where these errors hide in churches today, and in your own heart.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: What Pelagius Taught Pelagius was a British monk who came to Rome around the year 400. He was grieved by the loose living of professing Christians. He blamed it on teaching that made men think they couldn’t obey. When he heard a bishop quote Augustine’s prayer, Give what thou commandest, and command what thou wilt, he couldn’t bear it. To him that prayer made men lazy. If God commands it, he reasoned, man must be able to do it. From there he and his followers, Celestius and later Julian of Eclanum, taught these things. Adam’s sin hurt only Adam, and his children only by a bad example. No guilt and no corruption pass down to us. Every baby is born as Adam was made, innocent and able to choose good or evil. A man can keep God’s law by his own will if he will only try. Some have lived without sin. Grace means outward helps. The gift of free will, the law, the teaching and example of Christ, and the pardon of past sins. It isn’t a power within that changes the heart. Augustine answered him in book after book. The church condemned Pelagianism at the Council of Carthage in 418 and again at the general Council of Ephesus in 431. It’s one of the oldest heresies the church has named, and it has never stayed buried.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: Answering Pelagianism We fell in Adam, not only like him Paul doesn’t say we sin because we copy Adam. He says Adam’s one sin made us sinners. For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. Romans 5:19 (KJV) Look at the two halves together. If Adam only set a bad example, then Christ only set a good one, and we’re saved by copying him. Pelagius loses the gospel the moment he loses the fall. Paul also says death reigned even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression ( Romans 5:14 ). Infants die. They've copied no one. David confessed that his sin went back further than his choices. Behold, I was shapen in iniquity ( Psalm 51:5 ). They being the root of all mankind, the guilt of this sin was imputed; and the same death in sin, and corrupted nature, conveyed to all their posterity descending from them by ordinary generation. Westminster Confession of Faith 6.3 A dead man needs life, not an example Scripture doesn’t say we’re weak or sick. It speaks of those who were dead in trespasses and sins ( Ephesians 2:1 ). Pelagius offers a drowning man a book on how to swim. Christ goes down into the water, brings up the body, and breathes into it. The carnal mind is enmity against God, Paul says, for it's not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be. So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God ( Romans 8:7-8 ). Ought doesn't mean can This was Pelagius’s strongest argument, so answer it carefully. God commands every man to love him with all his heart. Does that prove every man is able? No. A man who has wasted his master’s money still owes the debt, though he can’t pay it. His inability is his own fault, so it doesn’t cancel his duty. Our inability isn’t like a man with no legs who wants to walk and can’t. It’s like a man who hates the road and won’t walk it. Ye will not come to me, that ye might have life ( John 5:40 ). Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil ( Jeremiah 13:23 ). God gives the law to stop every mouth and to show us our sin, for by the law is the knowledge of sin ( Romans 3:20 ). The law exposes our sin and sends us to Christ for righteousness. If we could, Christ died for nothing For if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain ( Galatians 2:21 ). If a man can keep the law by trying, the cross was a tragedy and not a rescue. Augustine’s prayer was right after all. God commands what we can’t do so that we’ll ask him for it. Then he gives what he commands. It's God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure ( Philippians 2:13 ).

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: The Halfway House After Pelagius was condemned, some monks in southern France tried a middle road. John Cassian and others taught that man isn’t dead in sin but badly sick. Grace is needed to finish salvation, but a sinner can often take the first step on his own. He can want to be healed, and God then helps him. Later writers called this Semi-Pelagianism. The Council of Orange in 529 rejected it. The council taught that even the beginning of faith, and the very desire to believe, is a gift of grace. It isn’t something in us by nature. Scripture agrees. No man can come unto me, except it were given unto him of my Father ( John 6:65 ). Flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, Jesus told Peter, but my Father which is in heaven ( Matthew 16:17 ). Most people who have never heard the word live in this halfway house. You’ll hear it in sayings like these. God has done ninety nine percent and you must do the last one. God votes for you, the devil votes against you, and you cast the deciding vote. They sound humble, but they leave the hinge of salvation in the sinner’s hand.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: What Arminianism Teaches Be fair here, because many who hold this view love Christ. Jacob Arminius was a Dutch pastor and later a professor at Leiden. He had studied at Geneva under Theodore Beza, Calvin’s successor. He died in 1609. The next year his followers set out their views in five articles called the Remonstrance. Conditional election. God chose to save those he foresaw would believe in Christ and keep believing. Universal atonement. Christ died for every man, gaining forgiveness for all, though only believers actually receive it. Man needs grace. Fallen man cannot of himself think, will, or do any saving good. He must be born again by God in Christ through the Spirit. Resistible grace. Grace begins, carries on, and finishes all good in us. But a man can refuse it to the end. Uncertain perseverance. The Remonstrants first said it needed more study whether a true believer could fall away. Their followers soon said he could. A century later John Wesley taught that God gives every person a prevenient grace, a grace that goes before. It doesn’t save anyone. But it lifts the fallen will enough that each man can accept Christ or refuse him. Arminians don’t all say the same thing. Wesleyans make much of prevenient grace. Some, often called Reformed Arminians, hold that a believer can be lost only by turning from Christ in unbelief. Others hold that God chose the church as a body in Christ rather than choosing persons. Many Baptists believe in conditional election and still hold that a true believer can't be lost. What follows answers what these views share, that the sinner’s response is what finally decides. It doesn’t claim every one of them is built the same way. Notice the third article. Arminians aren’t Pelagians. Most believe in the fall, in man’s need of grace, in Christ’s death in the place of sinners, and in justification by faith. Wesley preached Christ to coal miners in the open air. Don’t paint an Arminian brother as a heretic. But see where the hinge falls. In this view grace makes salvation possible for all, and the sinner’s own choice makes it actual for some. Grace is needed, but it doesn’t decide. So ask why one man believed and his neighbor didn’t. The final answer is something in the man. That’s where Paul’s principle in 1 Corinthians 4:7 presses hardest. That’s why the Reformed churches couldn’t let it pass.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: How the Church Answered The Dutch churches called the Synod of Dort. It met in 1618 and 1619, with delegates from Britain, Germany, and Switzerland. It answered the five articles of the Remonstrance point by point. Those answers are what people now call the five points of Calvinism. They were never meant to be the whole Reformed faith. They're a reply to five errors about how God saves. A generation later the Westminster Confession taught the same things in its own words. Here they are, answered from Scripture, in the order the Remonstrants raised them. God chose freely, not by foreseen faith According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, Ephesians 1:4-5 (KJV) He chose us that we should be holy, not because he saw we would be. And the cause is the good pleasure of his will. Paul says the same of Jacob and Esau, chosen before they were born, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth ( Romans 9:11 ). So then it's not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy ( Romans 9:16 ). If election hung on foreseen faith, Paul would have said so here. It would have answered every objection he raises in Romans 9 in one sentence. Luke gives the order plainly. As many as were ordained to eternal life believed ( Acts 13:48 ). He doesn’t say as many as believed were ordained. Arminians point to Romans 8:29 , For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate. But notice the word whom. God foreknew persons, not their choices. In Scripture to know often means to set your love on someone. God said to Israel, You only have I known of all the families of the earth ( Amos 3:2 ). He knew about every nation. He had chosen only one. And if God only looked ahead and saw who would believe, then he didn’t really choose anyone. He only noticed. Those of mankind that are predestinated unto life, God, before the foundation of the world was laid, according to His eternal and immutable purpose, and the secret counsel and good pleasure of His will, hath chosen, in Christ, unto everlasting glory, out of His mere free grace and love, without any foresight of faith, or good works, or perseverance in either of them, or any other thing in the creature, as conditions, or causes moving Him thereunto; and all to the praise of His glorious grace. Westminster Confession of Faith 3.5 Faith itself is a gift The Arminian says God chose those who would believe. But where does the believing come from? For unto you it's given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer for his sake ( Philippians 1:29 ). Faith is given. If God gives the faith, he can’t have chosen us because of the faith he planned to give. Christ died to save, not to make salvation possible The angel didn’t say Jesus would make salvation available. He said, he shall save his people from their sins ( Matthew 1:21 ). Christ said, I lay down my life for the sheep ( John 10:15 ). Then he told some who stood there, ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep ( John 10:26 ). On the night before he died he said, I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me ( John 17:9 ). That verse is about his prayer that night, so don’t lean on it alone. But dying and praying are two parts of one priestly work. The high priest offered the sacrifice and then carried the names of the tribes in before God. Christ by his own blood entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption ( Hebrews 9:12 ), and he ever liveth to make intercession for them that come unto God by him ( Hebrews 7:25 ). He died that they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance ( Hebrews 9:15 ). So it’s a fair question, drawn from his whole work as priest. Would he shed his blood for those he wouldn't bring by name before the Father? Paul builds assurance on this very point. Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died ( Romans 8:34 ). If Christ died for every man, and many men are condemned, that argument falls apart. If Christ paid for the sins of a man who is in hell, then God punishes the same sins twice. Answer that the man is punished for his unbelief, and you must ask whether Christ paid for that sin too. The Arminian cross makes salvation possible for everyone and certain for no one. The Reformed churches have never said Christ’s death is too small. It’s of infinite worth, enough for the whole world. And Christ is to be freely offered to every sinner who hears. The question isn’t how much his blood is worth. It’s what he meant to do when he shed it, and whether he did it. The Spirit’s call raises the dead Men do resist the Holy Ghost. Stephen said so ( Acts 7:51 ). Every sinner resists the outward call of the gospel as long as he’s left to himself. But God promised more than an offer. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them. Ezekiel 36:26-27 (KJV) Read the verbs. I'll give, I'll take away, I'll put, and cause you to walk. Ezekiel's verbs express God's saving action with certainty. Jesus said the same. No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day. John 6:44 (KJV) Everyone who is drawn in that verse is raised up at the end. So the drawing isn’t a grace given to all that many refuse. It brings the sinner all the way home. Arminians answer with John 12:32 , I'll draw all men unto me. Read the verses before it. Greeks had just come asking to see Jesus ( John 12:20-21 ). He says the cross will draw not only Jews but men of every nation. And Scripture never describes Wesley’s prevenient grace, a grace that lifts every man halfway and leaves the last step to him. It shows us Lydia, whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul ( Acts 16:14 ). This isn’t God dragging a man against his will. It’s God giving him a new will. Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power ( Psalm 110:3 ). All those whom God hath predestinated unto life, and those only, He is pleased, in His appointed and accepted time, effectually to call, by His Word and Spirit, out of that state of sin and death, in which they are by nature, to grace and salvation, by Jesus Christ; enlightening their minds spiritually and savingly to understand the things of God, taking away their heart of stone, and giving unto them an heart of flesh; renewing their wills, and, by His almighty power, determining them to that which is good, and effectually drawing them to Jesus Christ: yet so, as they come most freely, being made willing by His grace. Westminster Confession of Faith 10.1 Those he saves, he keeps If salvation hung on my will at the start, it would hang on my will to the end, and I’d fall. But Christ says of his sheep, they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand ( John 10:28 ). He that hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ ( Philippians 1:6 ). Believers are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ( 1 Peter 1:5 ). Paul’s golden chain has no missing links. Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified. Romans 8:30 (KJV) No one drops out between called and glorified. The warnings in Hebrews are real. They’re one of the means God uses to keep his people running. They aren’t a sign that he will let go. See Kept to the End .

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: What Free Will Really Is The Reformed faith doesn’t say man has no will, or that he is a puppet. Every man chooses what he most wants. Nothing outside him forces him. The trouble is inside. His wants are bent away from God, so he won’t choose God. Man, by his fall into a state of sin, hath wholly lost all ability of will to any spiritual good accompanying salvation: so as, a natural man, being altogether averse from that good, and dead in sin, is not able, by his own strength, to convert himself, or to prepare himself thereunto. Westminster Confession of Faith 9.3 The Confession traces the will through four estates. Adam in innocence was free to do good and able to fall. Fallen man still makes real choices, and he can do things that are outwardly good. He can love his children, keep his word, and serve his town. But apart from God’s grace he can’t choose any spiritual good that goes with salvation. Even his best deeds don’t come from a heart made clean by faith. So they can’t please God or earn his favor ( WCF 16.7 ). The converted man is freed to do good, though sin still clings to him. The saint in glory will be free to do good alone and never fall again ( WCF 9.2-5 ). Notice that the freest will of all, in heaven, can’t choose evil. Freedom in Scripture isn’t standing in the middle of the road with equal power to go either way. It’s being made what you were meant to be. Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin. If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed ( John 8:34 , 36).

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: The “All” and “World” Verses Arminians lean on a handful of verses with the word all or world in them. Take them seriously. Every word in them is true. The question is what each word means where it stands. You settle that the way you settle any word, by its context. The meaning must be established from grammar and context. How to Read the Bible Rightly says more. World does not always mean every person. When the Pharisees said, behold, the world is gone after him ( John 12:19 ), they didn’t mean every human being. That only shows the word can be used more than one way. It doesn’t settle what it means in a given verse. For that, look at the verses themselves. Read John 3:16 with Nicodemus. Jesus was speaking to a teacher of Israel. The Jews of that day looked for God’s mercy to rest on Israel. God so loved the world tells him it reaches past Israel to sinners of every people. The wonder is also in what the world is, a world in rebellion against its Maker. And the very next verses divide that world into two. He that believeth on him is not condemned, Jesus says, but he that believeth not is condemned already ( John 3:18 ). Reformed teachers read this verse as God’s love for the world in its sin and in its breadth, and as a sincere call to whosoever believeth. Read 1 John 2:2 with John 11 . John says Christ is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world. John used almost the same words once before. Caiaphas prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation, And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad ( John 11:51-52 ). There the whole world beyond Israel means God’s children scattered among the nations. Ask what propitiation means. A propitiation doesn’t merely make it possible for God’s wrath to be turned away. It actually turns it away. If Christ was in that sense the propitiation for every person who ever lived, then wrath is turned away from people who will still bear it. Read the way John 11 suggests, the verse holds together. Christ’s death turns away God’s wrath from his people in every nation, not from John’s first readers only. Look at who is addressed. 2 Peter 3:9 says God is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish. Peter wrote to them that have obtained like precious faith ( 2 Peter 1:1 ). God delays the end so that all his people will be brought in. Look at the verses around it. 1 Timothy 2:4 says God will have all men to be saved. Paul had just told Timothy that prayers be made for all men. Then he named some of them. For kings, and for all that are in authority ( 1 Timothy 2:1-2 ). He means men of every rank, even the rulers who persecute the church. Hold God’s sincere call as well. As I live, saith the Lord God , I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked ( Ezekiel 33:11 ). Reformed teachers have always held that God’s plea to sinners is real. He takes no delight in their ruin. His command and his plea go out to all. His secret decree is his own ( Deuteronomy 29:29 ). Don’t let a system make you mute where Scripture pleads.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: Questions People Ask Doesn’t that make us robots? No. A robot doesn’t want anything. A believer comes to Christ wanting to come, more willingly than he ever did anything. God doesn’t go around the will. He changes it. Paul tells you to work out your own salvation with fear and trembling. In the same breath he says it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do ( Philippians 2:12-13 ). Both are true at once. Isn’t it unfair? Fairness would send us all to hell. No one in hell will be there for want of being chosen. He will be there for sins he loved. God wrongs no one by showing mercy to some. I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy ( Romans 9:15 ). If God Chooses, Is He Fair? takes up this question at length. Then why evangelize? Because God saves through preaching. How shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? ( Romans 10:14 ). When Paul was afraid in Corinth, the Lord told him to keep speaking, for I have much people in this city ( Acts 18:10 ). Election was the reason he stayed. If salvation hung on how persuasive you are, you’d be crushed. Since it hangs on God, you can speak boldly and leave the result to him. Then why pray? Listen to an Arminian pray for his lost son. He doesn’t ask God to make salvation possible for the boy. He asks God to save him, to open his eyes and change his heart. On his knees he prays like a Calvinist. Keep praying exactly that way. God has bound himself to work through the prayers of his people.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: Is an Arminian My Brother? How to Spot Real Heresy sorts disagreements into heresy, serious error, and differences among the faithful. Here is where these views fall. Pelagianism is heresy. It denies original sin and our need of inward grace, and it makes Christ an example instead of a Savior. The church has condemned it for sixteen centuries. A man who teaches it, knowingly, after patient correction, isn’t preaching the gospel. Semi-Pelagianism was condemned at Orange, because it puts the start of salvation in man. It’s a deep error that leans hard toward the first. Arminianism is a serious error. It touches the doctrine of grace itself, so it weighs more than a difference over church government. The Synod of Dort removed Remonstrant ministers from their pulpits. The Westminster Confession denies its points one by one. But an Arminian who rests on Christ alone for his justification hasn’t denied the gospel. He is inconsistent, and happily so. His heart and his prayers are often better than his system. Some who began as Arminians have gone further. Open theism teaches that God doesn’t know what men will freely choose tomorrow. That’s no longer a question about grace. It’s a different God from the one who declares the end from the beginning ( Isaiah 46:10 ). Don’t lump an ordinary Arminian believer in with that. Remember the history. George Whitefield and John Wesley quarreled sharply over these very doctrines, and Whitefield didn’t back down. Yet he asked that Wesley preach his funeral sermon, and Wesley did. Charles Spurgeon could say Calvinism is the gospel and nothing else. Yet he still honored Wesley’s holiness and counted many Arminians as dear children of God.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
section: How to Talk With an Arminian Friend
text: How to Talk With an Arminian Friend In 1784 a young Charles Simeon met the aged John Wesley. Simeon asked whether he felt himself so depraved that he would never have turned to God if God hadn't first put it into his heart. Wesley said yes. Whether he looked for salvation only through the blood and righteousness of Christ. Yes, solely through Christ. Whether he was to save himself afterward by his own works. No, he must be saved by Christ from first to last. Whether he was upheld every moment by God, as an infant in its mother’s arms. Yes, altogether. Then Simeon said, in effect, that this was all his Calvinism, and that they should rejoice in what they shared. Simeon didn’t give up the doctrine. He showed Wesley that his heart already held it. That’s the best way to begin. Find out what he means. Many Christians say free will and mean only that they really chose and weren’t forced. You agree. Ask before you argue. Start with what you share. Christ’s deity, his death in our place, his rising, justification by faith. Say it out loud. It changes the temperature. Ask Simeon’s questions. Would you have come to God if he hadn’t first moved your heart? Will you keep yourself to the end, or must he keep you? Ask how he prays. Do you thank God for your faith? If you supplied it, why thank him? When you pray for a lost friend, what exactly do you ask God to do? Ask the hard question gently. You and your friend heard the same gospel. You believed and he didn’t. Why? Were you wiser, humbler, or more willing than he? Most believers won’t say yes. That refusal is the doctrine of grace in seed form. Open one passage together. John 6:35-65 is the best place to start. Read it slowly and ask what each verse says about who comes and why. Be patient. Many Reformed believers were Arminians first, and it took them years. The servant of the Lord must not strive, Paul says, but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient ( 2 Timothy 2:24 ). He corrects in hope, if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth ( 2 Timothy 2:25 ). If you believe God opens hearts, you don’t need to force one open. Do not lead with it to an unbeliever. A lost man needs Christ crucified, not the five points. Tell him to come, and tell him Christ won’t cast him out. How to Disagree With Another Christian has more on doing this well.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: Don't Overcorrect There’s a ditch on the other side of the road. Hyper-Calvinism says we mustn't call every sinner to repent and believe, or that a man needs some sign he is chosen before he may come. That isn’t the Reformed faith. The Confession says God freely offereth unto sinners life and salvation by Jesus Christ ( WCF 7.3 ). God now commandeth all men every where to repent ( Acts 17:30 ). Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth ( Isaiah 45:22 ). Spurgeon fought the hyper-Calvinists of his day as hard as he fought the Arminians. There’s another ditch, the proud Calvinist. Some men learn the doctrines of grace and become the least gracious men in the church. That’s a sad contradiction. If you really believe you added nothing to your salvation, you have nothing to sneer about. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth ( 1 Corinthians 8:1 ). A man who boasts in sovereign grace hasn’t yet understood it.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: Where It Hides Today Few churches today would call themselves Pelagian, but its ideas are everywhere. Moralism. God helps those who help themselves. Good people go to heaven. Be a better person and God will be pleased. That first saying isn’t in the Bible. God is the one that justifieth the ungodly ( Romans 4:5 ). Revival by technique. Charles Finney, the great revivalist of the 1800s, denied that we inherit a sinful nature from Adam. He preached a sermon titled Sinners Bound to Change Their Own Hearts. He taught that a revival is a purely philosophical result of the right use of the constituted means. In plain words, use the right methods and you’ll get converts. Many of the methods he spread are still used, and so is the belief behind them. Decisionism. Calling sinners to come to Christ now is right. Now is the day of salvation ( 2 Corinthians 6:2 ). But telling a man he’s saved because he walked an aisle or repeated a prayer puts his assurance in his act, not in Christ. Point him to Christ, and let the fruit show over time. Pressure. Pleading is biblical. We pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God ( 2 Corinthians 5:20 ). Working on people’s feelings with music and repetition until hands go up isn’t. If the Spirit gives new birth, you don’t need to manufacture it. Half truths. God has done all he can, and now it’s up to you. Jesus is a gentleman and won’t force himself on anyone. There’s a grain of truth here, since God doesn’t drag the unwilling. But he can make the unwilling willing, and he does. When you hear these things, don’t storm out. Test them by Scripture and speak to your elders. Remember that the people saying them often mean well. See How to Spot a False Teacher for when the problem goes deeper.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
section: The Pelagian in Your Own Heart
text: The Pelagian in Your Own Heart Pelagianism is a system of doctrine, and no baby is born holding a system. But the fallen heart naturally wants to take credit for its own righteousness. Its religion is always do and live. Even a man who confesses sovereign grace can fall into Pelagian ways of thinking. He can live as if his standing with God rose and fell with his performance. Watch for these signs in yourself. Your assurance goes up on good days and down on bad ones. Then you are resting on yourself, not on Christ. You look down on weaker believers. The Pharisee thanked God that I am not as other men are ( Luke 18:11 ), and went home unjustified. You secretly think you were wiser to believe. Go back to 1 Corinthians 4:7 . You pray little. A man who thinks he can manage doesn’t cry for help. You despair after a fall. If your salvation rested on you, despair would make sense. It doesn’t, so get up and go to Christ again. The cure isn’t to try less. It’s to know where your strength comes from. Paul worked harder than all the apostles, and then he caught himself. But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me. 1 Corinthians 15:10 (KJV)

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: Salvation Is of the Lord Jonah learned it in the belly of a fish. Salvation is of the Lord ( Jonah 2:9 ). Not mostly of the Lord with a little help. Of the Lord. That’s why the doctrines of grace aren’t cold. They mean the Father chose you, the Son died for you by name, and the Spirit raised you when you were dead. They mean you’ll be kept, because the one who began the work doesn’t quit. And they mean every crown in heaven gets thrown at his feet. Charles Wesley, John’s brother and an Arminian too, couldn't help singing it. In his hymn And Can It Be, his spirit lay “fast bound in sin and nature’s night” until God’s eye shone into the cell. “I woke, the dungeon flamed with light.” Then “my chains fell off, my heart was free.” That isn’t a man who decided. That’s a prisoner God set loose. If you’re not sure you’re chosen, don’t start there. Start with Christ’s open door. All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out. John 6:37 (KJV) No one ever came to him and found the door shut. The gospel tells you how to come today, and How God Saves Sinners sets out the doctrines of grace in brief.

title: How to Answer Arminianism and Pelagianism
text: Check the Historical Claim The Council of Orange in AD 529 rejected the claim that the beginning of faith springs from unaided human nature. Read the Canons of Orange , especially canons 3-5, alongside Scripture. This historical council isn't the doctrinal standard of Gentle King. The original Westminster Confession and the Word of God govern the teaching here.

title: How to Weigh “God Told Me”
text: God has spoken in his Son. How God guides you now, how to test a claimed word, and how to answer a friend kindly.

title: How to Weigh “God Told Me”
section: God Has Spoken in His Son
text: God Has Spoken in His Son God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds; Hebrews 1:1-2 (KJV) God once spoke by dreams, visions, and prophets. Then he spoke last and fullest by his Son. The Confession says God committed his word wholly unto writing, those former ways of God’s revealing his will unto his people being now ceased ( WCF 1.1 ). That written Word is enough. It makes the man of God perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works ( 2 Timothy 3:16-17 ). It’s the faith which was once delivered unto the saints (Jude 3), once for all. The whole counsel of God, concerning all things necessary for his own glory, man’s salvation, faith, and life, is either expressly set down in Scripture, or by good and necessary consequence may be deduced from Scripture: unto which nothing at any time is to be added, whether by new revelations of the Spirit, or traditions of men. Westminster Confession of Faith 1.6 The Bible closes with a warning against anyone who shall add unto the words of the prophecy of this book ( Revelation 22:18-19 ). Read fairly, it guards the book of Revelation itself. But it echoes what God said through Moses, Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you ( Deuteronomy 4:2 ). No man may add to what God has said. And see who that last Word is. The Son, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high ( Hebrews 1:3 ). You need no fresh message to know God’s heart toward sinners. If you’ve never come to Christ, start with the gospel .

title: How to Weigh “God Told Me”
text: Prophecy, Tongues, and Miracles Reformed churches hold that prophecy and tongues, as gifts that brought new words from God, have ceased. They belonged to the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone ( Ephesians 2:20 ). A foundation is laid once. The wonders of that time confirmed the apostles’ word ( Hebrews 2:3-4 ), and Paul calls them the signs of an apostle ( 2 Corinthians 12:12 ). Some evangelicals differ. They believe these gifts continue, and most say any prophecy today can be mistaken and must be tested by the Bible. Many of them love Christ, and this isn’t a line between the saved and the lost. But a word that may be wrong isn’t what the prophets meant by Thus saith the Lord . Call an impression an impression. God hasn’t stopped working. He still heals in answer to prayer ( James 5:14-16 ), and he is free to work without, above, and against means ( WCF 5.3 ). But an answered prayer is providence, not new revelation, and it makes no one an apostle. False prophets also shall shew signs and wonders ( Mark 13:22 ). A wonder never proves a message.

title: How to Weigh “God Told Me”
text: How God Guides You Now Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path ( Psalm 119:105 ). The psalm describes how God’s written Word guides us along the way. His Word. Most choices are already answered. Be honest, keep yourself pure, honor your parents, and marry only in the Lord ( 1 Corinthians 7:39 ). His providence. A man’s heart deviseth his way, but the Lord directeth his steps ( Proverbs 16:9 ). Wisdom. Where Scripture leaves you free, ask. If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God ( James 1:5 ). Counsel. In the multitude of counsellors there is safety ( Proverbs 11:14 ). The Spirit in the Word. The Confession says the inward illumination of the Spirit is necessary to understand what is revealed in the Word ( WCF 1.6 ). The Spirit opens your eyes to what is written. He doesn’t whisper what isn’t. So may you say the Lord led you? Yes. Looking back on a closed door, you may thankfully say so. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths ( Proverbs 3:6 ). That confesses providence and claims no message. “I believe the Lord has led me here” is humble. “God told me, so you must accept it” claims a prophet’s authority.

title: How to Weigh “God Told Me”
text: Test Every Claimed Word Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world. 1 John 4:1 (KJV) Moses gave Israel two tests. A prophet whose sign came true but who said, Let us go after other gods, was not to be heard ( Deuteronomy 13:1-5 ). A word can come true and still be false. And when a word spoken in the Lord ’s name didn't come to pass, he had not spoken it. Thou shalt not be afraid of him ( Deuteronomy 18:21-22 ). The Bereans checked even Paul against the scriptures ( Acts 17:11 ). Does it contradict Scripture? Refuse it, even from an angel from heaven ( Galatians 1:8 ). Does it add to Scripture? Refuse a new doctrine, duty, or rule for others too ( WCF 1.6 ). Does it agree with Scripture? Then obey the Scripture. The claim adds nothing. Did it fail? Then God didn’t speak it. Don’t fear it. Dreams, Impressions, and Feelings A dream now is a dream. Jeremiah set a dream beside God’s word and asked, What is the chaff to the wheat? ( Jeremiah 23:28 ). A strong feeling or a sense of peace may be God stirring you toward a duty he already commanded. It may also be your own wishes or fears. The heart is deceitful above all things ( Jeremiah 17:9 ). So these things can’t bind your conscience or anyone else’s. God alone is Lord of the conscience, and he binds it by his Word ( WCF 20.2 ). Weigh impressions by Scripture, never Scripture by impressions.

title: How to Weigh “God Told Me”
section: When a Friend Says “God Told Me”
text: When a Friend Says “God Told Me” Most who say it aren’t false prophets. They usually mean they prayed and came away with a strong sense. Be kind. Don’t mock, and don’t pounce. Ask what he means. “How did God tell you?” Often it was an impression in prayer. Agree with what Scripture says. If he says God wants him to forgive his brother, say amen and show him the verse. Point him to the surer word. Peter heard the Father’s voice on the holy mount, yet he wrote, We have also a more sure word of prophecy ( 2 Peter 1:16-19 ). Leave room on lesser choices. If he says God told him to take a job, you needn’t argue. Encourage him to hold it as his judgment under God. Be firmer when a word is used to control. Someone may say God told him you must marry him, give him money, keep quiet about how he treats you, or obey him without question. Then he’s laying a yoke God never laid. To require absolute and blind obedience is to destroy liberty of conscience ( WCF 20.2 ). You may say no. Tell your elders. If a leader does this, read How to Spot a False Teacher . If someone is hurting you, read If You Are Not Safe .

title: How to Weigh “God Told Me”
text: This Week Read Hebrews 1 and 2 Peter 1 . Notice what God calls sure. Take one decision in front of you. Write down what Scripture says about it. Pray for wisdom, and ask a wise believer. Watch your words. Instead of “God told me,” say what happened. “I prayed and have come to believe this,” or “This verse convicted me.” Lay down a false burden. If a word frightens or binds you, weigh it by Scripture with an elder. Rest in the Son. God’s last Word to you is Christ, and he is enough.

title: How to Test Books, Music, and Preachers Online
text: Testing teaching online, your own elders, worship music, books and films, and your time and attention.

title: How to Test Books, Music, and Preachers Online
text: Every Believer Must Discern Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world. 1 John 4:1 (KJV) John wrote that to ordinary church members. The Bereans searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so, and they did it with an apostle ( Acts 17:11 ). Paul told a young church to prove all things and hold fast that which is good ( 1 Thessalonians 5:21 ). Discernment is a skill that grows with use. Hebrews speaks of those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil ( Hebrews 5:14 ). The writer pictures a man whose senses are trained by practice. A Christian who never tests what he hears stays a child. And the voices now reach you in your pocket all day long.

title: How to Test Books, Music, and Preachers Online
text: Testing Teaching Online A book, a podcast, a video, or a sermon from another church is tested the same way as a preacher in a pulpit. Hold it up to Scripture, and use the Westminster Standards as a faithful summary of what Scripture teaches. The Larger Catechism tells hearers to examine what they hear by the Scriptures ( WLC 160 ). Use the seven questions in How to Spot a False Teacher . The last of them, who holds him to account, matters most online, where anyone with a camera can build a following. Your Own Elders Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you. Hebrews 13:17 (KJV) A teacher you’ve never met can’t watch for your soul. He doesn’t know your name, and he won’t give account for you. Christ gave pastors and teachers to his church for the perfecting of the saints ( Ephesians 4:11-12 ), and he gives them through a local church. A sound teacher online can help. When he becomes the voice you trust over your own elders, something has gone wrong. Let the sermon you hear on the Lord’s Day be the main meal of your week, and the rest a side dish. What the Feed Feeds You The apps that serve you videos are built to keep you watching. They learn what stirs you, and they bring you more of it. If outrage or flattery keeps you watching, you’ll get more outrage and flattery. Paul warned of people who, after their own lusts, heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears ( 2 Timothy 4:3 ). A feed can do the heaping for you. Choose what you listen to on purpose. Don’t let a machine choose it for you.

title: How to Test Books, Music, and Preachers Online
text: Worship Music and Other Songs In the public worship of God, he decides what is sung. This site holds, with the Reformed Presbyterian churches, that God gave the Psalms to be sung in worship, without instruments. How God Wants to Be Worshiped explains why. Listening at home or in the car is a different matter. Many in Reformed churches listen to songs about God outside of worship. Others hold that any singing of praise to God is worship, and keep to the Psalms in private as well. Either way, test what you take in. Are the words true? Read the lyrics on their own, without the music. Would they stand if a minister said them from the pulpit? Is there theology in them? Do they say who God is, what Christ has done, and what sin is? Or could you sing them to a girlfriend by changing one word? What does it stir? Music moves the feelings. That’s a gift. Ask whether it stirs love for Christ and hatred of sin, or only a mood you mistake for God’s presence.

title: How to Test Books, Music, and Preachers Online
text: Books, Music, Films, and Games Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things. Philippians 4:8 (KJV) Not all culture is evil. Paul quoted the pagan poets to the Athenians ( Acts 17:28 ). Good stories, honest history, and beautiful music can be enjoyed with thanks. God alone is Lord of the conscience ( WCF 20.2 ), and no one may bind you with rules Scripture doesn’t give. But liberty isn’t license. They who, upon pretense of Christian liberty, do practice any sin, or cherish any lust, do thereby destroy the end of Christian liberty ( WCF 20.3 ). David said, I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes ( Psalm 101:3 ). Paul said to have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, for it's a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret ( Ephesians 5:11-12 ). Scripture itself tells of wicked deeds, so a story may show sin. The question is whether it shows sin to be hated or serves it up to be enjoyed. The Larger Catechism names lascivious songs, books, pictures, and stage plays among the sins of the seventh commandment ( WLC 139 ). Nudity and sex on a screen aren’t a matter of taste. What does it make me love? Does it make evil look good, or good look foolish? Does it rule me? All things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any ( 1 Corinthians 6:12 ). Can I do it in faith? Whatsoever is not of faith is sin ( Romans 14:23 ). If your conscience is uneasy, leave it. Films that portray Christ raise a further question. The Larger Catechism counts any representation of any of the three persons of God a sin against the second commandment ( WLC 109 ), and an actor playing Jesus is such a representation.

title: How to Test Books, Music, and Preachers Online
text: Your Time and Your Attention See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Ephesians 5:15-16 (KJV) Your hours belong to God. A show can be clean and still steal an evening that was owed to prayer, to your wife, or to your children. The Larger Catechism calls for a sober use of recreations and counts their immoderate use a sin ( WLC 135 , 136). Many believers don’t lack time to pray. They spend it on a screen a few minutes at a time. If you find you can’t put the phone down, that’s not a small thing. It has brought you under its power. Confess it, and take steps. If the screen has led you into pornography, read the part on the eyes . Guiding Children and Teens Parents must guide what their children watch, hear, and read, and teach them to test it themselves. Watch with them, and ask afterward what the story made them admire. Go first. Children learn more from what you scroll than from what you say. See Phones and Screens in the parenting guide.

title: How to Test Books, Music, and Preachers Online
text: This Week List your voices. Write down every teacher and channel you follow. Run each through the seven questions. Ask your elders. Tell your pastor who you listen to and ask what he thinks. Let him be the teacher you hear most. Read the lyrics. Take the songs you play most and read the words alone. Keep what’s true. Check your screen time. Compare last week’s hours on the phone with your hours in prayer and the Word. Then keep it off at the table and at bedtime. Bring it to Christ. Where you’ve fed on what grieves him, confess it. The blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin ( 1 John 1:7 ). If you’ve never come to him, start with the gospel .

title: How to Disagree With Another Christian
text: Three kinds of difference, Romans 14 in practice, how to disagree well, and when to let it go.

title: How to Disagree With Another Christian
text: Three Kinds of Difference Christians will disagree until Christ comes. First know what kind of disagreement you’re in, because Scripture doesn’t treat them all alike. Matters of the faith. Who God is, who Christ is, and how a sinner is saved. To deny these is heresy, and you must earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints (Jude 3). How to Spot Real Heresy sets out where that line runs. Serious error. A brother is wrong on something Scripture teaches that matters, such as baptism, worship, or the government of the church. But he doesn’t deny the gospel. Hold your ground, and still own him as a brother in Christ. Some questions of interpretation sit near here, such as the thousand years of Revelation 20 . Faithful Reformed men have read them differently (see Prophecy ). Matters of conscience and wisdom. Things Scripture neither commands nor forbids. Here God has left believers free. God alone is Lord of the conscience, and hath left it free from the doctrines and commandments of men which are in anything contrary to his Word, or beside it, in matters of faith or worship. Westminster Confession of Faith 20.2 To tell which you’re in, ask two questions. Does this touch the gospel itself? Does Scripture command or forbid this, either in plain words or by good and necessary consequence ( WCF 1.6 )? If not, it’s a matter of liberty, like whether to drink wine ( Alcohol ). Some questions sit where faithful believers weigh Scripture’s principles differently, such as tattoos ( Tattoos ) or the spacing of children ( Birth Control ). Wisdom still applies, but leave room where God leaves room. Treat your opinions as gospel and you become a Pharisee. Treat the gospel as opinion and you have nothing left to stand on.

title: How to Disagree With Another Christian
text: Romans 14 in Practice Rome was divided over food and holy days, and Paul told both sides how to treat each other. Let not him that eateth despise him that eateth not; and let not him which eateth not judge him that eateth: for God hath received him. Romans 14:3 (KJV) The strong brother knows the thing is lawful. His temptation is to despise the tender conscience. The weak brother thinks a lawful thing is sin. His temptation is to judge the other as worldly. Paul forbids both. Each will answer to his own master ( Romans 14:4 , 10-12). Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind ( Romans 14:5 ). Settle it before God, and never push a brother to act against his conscience, for whatsoever is not of faith is sin ( Romans 14:23 ). Love sets limits on liberty. Destroy not him with thy meat, for whom Christ died ( Romans 14:15 ). If your freedom would lead a brother to sin against his conscience, lay it down ( 1 Corinthians 8:9-13 ). Christ laid down far more for you. Yet bearing with a weaker brother isn’t the same as letting any man make his scruple a law for the church. Paul wouldn't have believers bound by Touch not, taste not, handle not, after the commandments and doctrines of men ( Colossians 2:20-22 ).

title: How to Disagree With Another Christian
text: How to Disagree Well Listen first. Be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath ( James 1:19 ). State his view so fairly that he would agree with it. Speak the truth in love ( Ephesians 4:15 ). Both halves. Truth without love is a club. Love without truth leaves him in his error. Don’t fight to win. Aim at his good and God’s truth. And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth; 2 Timothy 2:24-25 (KJV) Assume the best. Charity believeth all things, hopeth all things ( 1 Corinthians 13:7 ). The Larger Catechism counts misconstructing intentions, words, and actions as a sin against the ninth commandment (Q&A 145). Read him in the kindest way his words honestly bear. Argue the point, not the man. No mocking, no labels, no guessing at motives. Remember you may be the one who is wrong ( Matthew 7:3-5 ).

title: How to Disagree With Another Christian
text: Two Quarrels in Scripture Paul and Barnabas Paul and Barnabas couldn’t agree whether to take John Mark again, since he had left them before. And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other ( Acts 15:39 ). It was a matter of wisdom, not doctrine, and Scripture doesn’t say who was right. But later Paul names Barnabas as a fellow worker ( 1 Corinthians 9:6 ) and tells the Colossians to receive Mark ( Colossians 4:10 ).
