text: The Grief Scripture Names This grief comes a month at a time, and the people around you may never know. Scripture names the barren womb among the things that are never satisfied, beside the grave ( Proverbs 30:15-16 ). Sarah waited for a son until she was old. Rachel was loved by her husband more than her sister was, and it didn’t ease the ache. And when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die. Genesis 30:1 (KJV) Jacob answered in anger, Am I in God’s stead? ( Genesis 30:2 ). It was true, but it wasn’t tender. Hannah’s rival mocked her year after year, until she wept, and did not eat ( 1 Samuel 1:7 ). Her husband asked, am not I better to thee than ten sons? ( 1 Samuel 1:8 ). He meant it kindly, but he didn’t understand. So Hannah prayed at the house of God until the priest thought she was drunk. And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord . 1 Samuel 1:15 (KJV) You may do the same. Hannah went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad ( 1 Samuel 1:18 ), before she had any answer at all. Her prayer didn’t change her womb that day. It changed where her grief was resting. Elisabeth grew old with no child ( Luke 1:7 ). When at last she conceived, she said God had taken away my reproach among men ( Luke 1:25 ). God had seen that shame, and he sees yours. Husbands, this is your grief too. Weep with your wife, and pray with her out loud. Not a Punishment Zacharias and Elisabeth were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless ( Luke 1:6 ). The next verse says they had no child. Scripture sets those facts side by side so that no one will join them as cause and effect. God did once close the wombs of a household in judgment ( Genesis 20:18 ), but he said so in his word. He hasn’t said it of you. When the disciples asked whose sin had made a man blind, Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents ( John 9:3 ). If that fear keeps coming back, read I think he is punishing me .

title: What the Bible Says About IVF and Infertility
text: A Gift, Not a Right Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord : and the fruit of the womb is his reward. Psalm 127:3 (KJV) A heritage is given, never owed. The longing for children is good, but no one has a right to a child, not even the most faithful couple in the church. A Christian may ask God for children with all his heart. He must still let God be the giver. A childless marriage is a whole marriage. They shall be one flesh ( Genesis 2:24 ), and God makes that union at the wedding, not at the birth of a child. Of the purposes the Confession gives for marriage, the mutual help of husband and wife comes first ( WCF 24.2 , and see Why God Gave It ). A husband and wife without children aren’t a family waiting to begin. They're a family. Seeking Help From Doctors God, in his ordinary providence, maketh use of means, yet is free to work without, above, and against them, at his pleasure. Westminster Confession of Faith 5.3 The skill of doctors is one of those means. Isaiah had a lump of figs laid on Hezekiah’s boil ( Isaiah 38:21 ), and Paul called Luke the beloved physician ( Colossians 4:14 ). The Larger Catechism counts a sober use of physic, or medicine, among the duties of the sixth commandment ( WLC 135 ). So tests to find the cause are lawful. So is surgery to repair what is damaged, and medicine to help a body work as it should. They show no more lack of faith than setting a broken arm. Treatments that help a husband’s seed reach his wife within her own body raise far fewer questions than IVF. And keep praying. Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren ( Genesis 25:21 ). Watch your heart too. Give me children, or else I die, can harden from a cry into a demand.

title: What the Bible Says About IVF and Infertility
section: What Is Wrong in IVF as It's Commonly Done
text: What Is Wrong in IVF as It's Commonly Done In IVF a woman takes drugs so that her body ripens many eggs at once. Doctors draw the eggs out and join them with sperm in a lab. The embryos grow for a few days. Then one or more are placed in the mother’s womb. Everything turns on what those embryos are. Scripture treats a human being as a person from conception, made in God’s image, as What God Says About the Unborn shows. An embryo in a dish isn’t a possible child. He is a child, very small. David said to God, Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect ( Psalm 139:16 ). Unperfect means not yet formed. God saw David at that size, and knew him. Measured by that, much of what clinics routinely do breaks the sixth commandment. Making more embryos than will be transferred. Children are made with the plan that some will never get a chance. Freezing them without end. Many are never claimed. A child is left neither allowed to grow nor allowed to die. Discarding them. Embryos judged weak or no longer wanted are thrown away or given for research. That is the taking of a human life. Testing to select. Clinics test embryos and transfer only those judged healthy, or of the sex the parents want. The rest are set aside. A child with a weakness bears God’s image as fully as any other ( Exodus 4:11 ). Selective reduction. When several babies begin to grow at once, doctors may offer to end some of their lives so others may be born. It is abortion. Each of these treats an image-bearer as material to be sorted, stored, and spent. The Larger Catechism forbids whatsoever else tends to the destruction of the life of any ( WLC 136 ). Donors and Surrogates Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh. Genesis 2:24 (KJV) Donor eggs, donor sperm, and a surrogate mother all bring a third person into what God made for two. Sarah gave Hagar to Abraham, and Rachel gave Bilhah to Jacob ( Genesis 16:1-4 , 30:3-4). Scripture records the jealousy and sorrow that followed. It never commends the choice. A Christian couple should refuse these, however strong the longing and however kind the offer. Where Faithful Teachers Differ Some couples ask about IVF within strict limits. They would use only the husband’s and wife’s own cells, and make only as many embryos as will all be transferred, with none frozen or discarded. Reformed ethicists differ on whether that can be done in good conscience. Many counsel against it. They note that it parts conceiving a child from the marriage bed (see Tenderness in the Marriage Bed ). They also note that once the process begins, clinics press hard for more embryos. Others permit it, with every limit kept and every embryo welcomed as a son or daughter. This page won’t settle what faithful teachers haven’t. Don't go near it without your elders’ counsel. Don't take one step your conscience can’t take before God. Whatsoever is not of faith is sin ( Romans 14:23 ).

title: What the Bible Says About IVF and Infertility
text: If You've Frozen Embryos If you've frozen embryos from earlier treatment, you face grave decisions about children already conceived. Those embryos are your children. So you may not have them destroyed, and you may not give them for research. Leaving them frozen forever isn’t a safe middle way. Christians have sought to give such children life in two ways. The first is to have them transferred to their own mother’s womb, even if you thought your family was complete, and even at great cost. The second, if that can’t be done, is embryo adoption. Another married couple receives them, and the wife carries them as her own. Some believers hesitate over this too. But it brings no third person into the making of a child. The child already exists and needs a mother to live, and many see it as a rescue. Not every embryo survives thawing, and not every transfer takes. When a child dies that way, it’s a real death to grieve, and not one you caused. If your baby died before birth is for you too. Don’t decide this alone. Go to your elders. Find out what your clinic will do if the fees stop, and make sure nothing is done without your word. Ask God for courage to do what is costly.

title: What the Bible Says About IVF and Infertility
text: Children Conceived by IVF If you were conceived by IVF, you're fully human and fully loved by God. You're no less precious than any other child. God saw you in a dish as clearly as he saw David in the womb, and you bear his image. God never counts a child less for how he came. Perez was born of Judah’s sin with Tamar, and he stands in the line of Christ ( Matthew 1:3 ). If brothers or sisters of yours were made with you and never born, you may grieve them. If a donor’s egg or sperm was used, you may mourn a parent you’ve never known. That isn’t ingratitude. God is a father of the fatherless ( Psalm 68:5 ), and you may bring all of it to him. Parents, if you used IVF without knowing what was wrong in it, you may confess the wrong without regretting your child. You can repent of how something was done and still thank God every day for the life he gave. If a donor was used, your child is still fully yours to raise. Love him without a shadow over him. He did nothing wrong by being born. Pardon for Embryos Destroyed Some of you agreed to let embryos be discarded, or tested and set aside, or reduced in the womb. Many were never told those were children. Some knew. Either way the guilt is real, and this page won’t call it nothing. Paul once hunted Christians to their death. Afterward he wrote, I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief ( 1 Timothy 1:13 ). Ignorance didn’t make his sin innocent, but he received mercy. If you knew what you were doing, there's mercy for that too, for Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners ( 1 Timothy 1:15 ). As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us. Psalm 103:12 (KJV) Christ bore the wrath of God for every sin of all who trust in him, and he rose from the dead. If you’ve never come to him, read The Gospel , and come today. Confess the sin by name, and believe him, for there is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus ( Romans 8:1 ). Leave those little ones with the Judge of all the earth, who will do right ( Genesis 18:25 ). If the guilt keeps returning, read What I did is too great to forgive .

title: What the Bible Says About IVF and Infertility
section: Adoption and the Family of Christ
text: Adoption and the Family of Christ Adoption Isn't Second Best Telling a grieving couple to "just adopt" treats adoption as a cure for their sorrow. An adopted child must be welcomed as a person to love, never as a replacement for someone lost. Adoption is a worthy and joyful way to welcome a child into a family. It’s the way God made his own. But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. Galatians 4:4-7 (KJV) Every Christian is adopted. God planned it before the world began, having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself ( Ephesians 1:5 ). We have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father ( Romans 8:15 ). An adopted son has a right to all the privileges of the sons of God ( WSC 34 ). He isn’t a lesser son in God’s house, nor in yours. Adoption and foster care carry real losses, for the child above all, and aren’t every couple’s calling. But they let a home show what God has done in Christ. If Children Never Come For some, no child will come, by birth or by adoption. God hasn’t passed you over. The eunuch could never have a child and feared he was a dry tree ( Isaiah 56:3 ). God made him a promise. For thus saith the Lord unto the eunuchs that keep my sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and take hold of my covenant; Even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off. Isaiah 56:4-5 (KJV) A dry tree pictures a life that bears no fruit and leaves nothing behind. In Israel a man’s name lived on through his sons. God answers that fear by saying he will keep yours himself, in his own house. When his mother and brothers came for him, Jesus looked at those around him and said, whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother ( Mark 3:35 ). In his church you aren’t on the edge of the family. There are children and young believers there who need a father or mother in the faith. Paul had no children, and he called Timothy my own son in the faith ( 1 Timothy 1:2 ). The ache may stay with you all your life, but it won’t have the last word. God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes ( Revelation 21:4 ).

title: What the Bible Says About IVF and Infertility
text: Where to Go From Here If You're Waiting for a Child Pour out your soul before the Lord , as Hannah did. You don’t need fine words. Talk with each other. Decide together, before you’re worn out, how far you will go with treatment and where you will stop. Ask your elders for counsel before any treatment beyond tests, surgery, and ordinary medicine. Refuse what is wrong, however it is offered. No embryos made to be frozen or discarded, no testing to select, no donors or surrogates, and never selective reduction. How the Church Should Care for the Infertile Weep with them that weep ( Romans 12:15 ). A baptism may be a hard day for someone near you. Keep rejoicing, but notice who is quiet. Stop asking when. You don’t know what a couple is carrying. And don’t hand out cures. Just relax, and just adopt, aren’t comfort. Pray with them instead. Remember Mother’s Day and Father’s Day. If your church marks these days at all, they can be the hardest of the year for the childless and the bereaved. Don’t ask every mother to stand. Pray also for those who long for children. Make room in the family. Bring childless couples into your home and your children’s lives as aunts and uncles in the faith. Stand by those who adopt and foster. Paul bowed his knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named ( Ephesians 3:14-15 ). If you're in Christ, you belong to that family now, with or without children of your own. He will bring you home.

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
text: Children are a heritage of the Lord. Teaching them, disciplining them, praying for them, and walking with them through the teen years.

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
text: Children and the Covenant Sign The original Westminster Confession teaches the baptism of children of believing parents ( WCF 28.4 ). Baptism places a child under the visible administration of the covenant, but parents must still teach that child to repent and trust Christ. See Baptism and Family Worship .

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
text: A Gift and a Covenant The world often counts children as a cost. God speaks of them another way. Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord : and the fruit of the womb is his reward. As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate. Psalm 127:3-5 (KJV) A heritage is given, not earned. Your children are lent to you by God, who owns them and will ask how you cared for them. The arrows are a picture, and what they picture is real. An arrow is shaped with care, aimed, and then let go. It was never meant to stay in the hand. For believers there's more. God promised Abraham to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee ( Genesis 17:7 ). That didn’t end when Christ came. At Pentecost Peter said, For the promise is unto you, and to your children ( Acts 2:39 ). So the sign of the covenant still belongs to the children of believers, as circumcision once did. Not only those that do actually profess faith in and obedience unto Christ, but also the infants of one or both believing parents are to be baptized. Westminster Confession of Faith 28.4 Our Baptist brothers baptize only those who profess faith, but this page holds with the Confession. Be clear about what baptism doesn’t do. It doesn’t make a child born again, and not all who are baptized are undoubtedly regenerated ( WCF 28.5 ). No parent can give a child a new heart. Salvation is of the Lord ( Jonah 2:9 ). The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit. John 3:8 (KJV) Listeth means pleases. You can’t command the wind, and you can’t command new birth. What you can do is raise your children where the Spirit has promised to work, under his Word and among his people. Don’t presume your child is saved because he was baptized. And don’t doubt that he may be saved because he is young. Call him, every day of his life, to repent and believe for himself.

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
section: Teaching Them in the Ordinary Day
text: Teaching Them in the Ordinary Day The great command, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, comes with a charge to parents fastened to it ( Deuteronomy 6:4-9 ). And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up. Deuteronomy 6:6-7 (KJV) Notice the order. The words are in your heart first, and then you teach them. A parent can’t pass on what he doesn’t have. Then notice where the teaching happens. It’s breakfast, and the drive to practice, and bedtime. Children learn from daily conversations as well as formal teaching. Speak of God and his Word at the table, on the way to school, and when you correct them. The language of binding God’s Word on hands and forehead calls families to obey it in their work and their thinking ( Deuteronomy 6:8 ). Reformed households have long leaned on three helps. The first is the Shorter Catechism, which sets the whole faith out in short answers a child can learn. What is the chief end of man? Man’s chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him for ever ( WSC 1 ). Ask what the answers mean. Keep at it into the teen years, when they begin to bear weight. The second is daily family worship . The third is keeping the Lord’s Day together. A child who sees his parents delight in that day learns something no lesson can teach.

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
text: Fathers, Mothers, and Children Fathers And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. Ephesians 6:4 (KJV) A father answers to God first for his household. Nurture is the training of a whole life. Admonition is the warning word, spoken in time. The warning to fathers comes first. Paul gives the reason elsewhere, lest they be discouraged ( Colossians 3:21 ). A child can be crushed by a father who is never pleased, who mocks, or who keeps none of the rules he makes. The Larger Catechism names among the sins of parents correcting their children unduly and provoking them to wrath ( WLC 130 ). A father who is absent while sitting in the same room discourages too. If your anger frightens your family, read the part on anger today. Mothers A mother’s teaching carries real authority. My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother ( Proverbs 1:8 ). Proverbs 31 opens with what a king’s mother taught him. It closes with a woman who rises while it's yet night for her household. In her tongue is the law of kindness, and her children arise up, and call her blessed ( Proverbs 31:1 , 15, 26, 28). Her strength is that she feareth the Lord ( Proverbs 31:30 ). Paul told Titus that older women should teach the younger to love their children and to be keepers at home ( Titus 2:3-5 ). It’s striking that love for children has to be taught. Older mothers have much to give younger ones. Keepers at home makes the home a mother’s first field of work. Faithful Reformed believers differ on how that bears on work outside it. But none may treat the home as an afterthought. Children Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth. Ephesians 6:1-3 (KJV) In the Lord means in all things lawful. No parent may command a child to sin, for we ought to obey God rather than men ( Acts 5:29 ). This is the fifth commandment, and the Larger Catechism opens it up ( WLC 123-133 ). Children owe their parents reverence and willing obedience. They're to bear with their parents’ weaknesses and cover them in love ( WLC 127 ). Parents owe their children love, prayer, teaching, correction, and a life worth following ( WLC 129 ). The commandment runs both ways. Even its promise of long life is given as far as it shall serve for God’s glory and their own good ( WLC 133 ). Some obedient children die young. Hold on to that for the part on Proverbs below. Discipline Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child ( Proverbs 22:15 ), as it is in ours, and a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame ( Proverbs 29:15 ). Eli was judged because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not ( 1 Samuel 3:13 ). Correct calmly and consistently, never in a rage and never to shame. Aim at the heart, and end with the child restored and held. The full treatment is in What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline .

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
text: Is Proverbs 22:6 a Promise? Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it. Proverbs 22:6 (KJV) Many parents read this verse as a guarantee. Then a son walks away from the faith at nineteen, and the verse becomes an accusation. Either God broke his word, or the parents broke the formula. Neither is true. The way out is to read the verse as the kind of writing it is. Taking the Bible literally means taking each part as it was meant to be taken. A psalm is a song, a law is a law, and a proverb is a proverb. Proverbs are wholly true, because they're God’s Word. But a proverb is a short saying that tells how God has ordered life to go as a rule. It doesn’t stop to list the exceptions. The book of Proverbs shows this itself. Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him. Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit. Proverbs 26:4-5 (KJV) Both are true, and no one can follow both at once. Wisdom knows which fits the fool in front of you. Or take the hand of the diligent maketh rich ( Proverbs 10:4 ). That’s how life usually goes, and a lazy man should hear it. Yet the same Bible says the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong ( Ecclesiastes 9:11 ). The fear of the Lord prolongeth days ( Proverbs 10:27 ), and yet righteous Abel’s days were cut short by his brother ( Genesis 4:8 , Matthew 23:35 ). None of these sayings is false. Each is a general truth of wisdom, and the rest of Scripture shows where it bends. So it's with Proverbs 22:6 . Receive Proverbs 22:6 as wisdom for faithful instruction, and read it alongside Scripture's accounts of faithful parents whose children went astray. God ordinarily uses faithful teaching in the home to bring children to himself. Many wanderers have come home late, carried back by words they heard at their mother’s table. Train your children with hope. But the verse isn’t a contract that makes a child’s salvation the wage of a parent’s work. It can’t be, because salvation is of the Lord. And Scripture shows it isn’t. Hezekiah did right though his father Ahaz didn’t, and his own son Manasseh did evil ( 2 Kings 16:2 , 18:3, 21:2). God himself said, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me ( Isaiah 1:2 ). That was no failure in his fathering. Reading the verse rightly guards against two sins. If your children walk with God, don’t take the credit. It was grace. Other parents did as much as you and are weeping tonight. If your child has wandered, don’t decide that God has broken his word. And don’t carry your child’s sin as your own ( Ezekiel 18:20 ). Confess where you did wrong, and keep praying. When Your Child Walks Away From the Lord is written for you.

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
text: The Teen Years The first chapters of Proverbs are mostly a father talking to a son on the edge of manhood. My son, he says, again and again. He warns him about friends who will entice him into violence for quick money ( Proverbs 1:10-19 ), and about the strange woman, whose lips drop as an honeycomb ( Proverbs 5:3 ). That’s the Bible’s picture of raising a teenager. It’s long and honest talk about what the world is about to press on him. The aim shifts in these years. You still require obedience while he lives under your roof. But now you’re reaching for the heart. My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways ( Proverbs 23:26 ). Obedience without the heart rarely survives the day he leaves. It may comfort you that Mary and Joseph didn’t understand their son at twelve, and he was without sin. He went home and was subject unto them, and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart ( Luke 2:48-51 ). Not understanding your teenager for a season isn’t always a sign that something is wrong. Talking and Listening Be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath ( James 1:19 ). He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him ( Proverbs 18:13 ). If you jump to the lecture the moment your daughter tells you something hard, she’ll stop telling you. Teens often open up late at night, or side by side in the car. Moses already named those times, when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down. Stay up for it. Phones and Screens A phone with the open internet puts the whole world in a child’s pocket, its foulest parts included. Scripture gives no age for a first phone, and Christian families draw the lines in different places. But David said, I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes ( Psalm 101:3 ). The Larger Catechism counts among the sins of parents careless exposing, or leaving them to wrong, temptation, and danger ( WLC 130 ). An unfiltered phone behind a closed bedroom door is exactly that. Keep screens out of bedrooms at night. Use filters, and tell your children why. Then go first. A father who scrolls through supper can’t tell his son to put the phone down. If your child is already caught in pornography, don’t explode. Help him fight it, and read the part on pornography together. Someone online may pressure them for pictures or threaten them. Tell your children they can come to you without shame if that happens. It’s a crime against them, and you should report it . Friends He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed. Proverbs 13:20 (KJV) Teenagers become like the friends they keep. Know their friends by name. Open your home and feed them, so your house is where they gather. Don’t only forbid bad company. Help them find good. Letting Go The goal isn’t a child who needs you forever. It’s a grown man or woman who fears God when you’re not in the room. A man shall leave his father and his mother ( Genesis 2:24 ), and the arrow was made to fly. Hannah brought Samuel to the house of the Lord when the child was young, and said, I have lent him to the Lord ( 1 Samuel 1:24-28 ). Every parent must give his children up to God in his own way. Hand over responsibility a little at a time while they're still at home, and move from command toward counsel. When they set up their own homes, the obedience of a child under your roof gives way. But the duty to honor never ends ( Mark 7:10-12 ). You become a counselor, not a ruler. That isn’t losing them. It’s what you were raising them for. Praying for Them Job’s children were grown and keeping their own houses, and still he rose up early in the morning and offered for every one of them. For Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts ( Job 1:5 ). You don’t know their hearts either. Pray for each by name every day. Pray for their souls first, and then for their purity and their future homes. Pray as Christ prayed for his own, not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil ( John 17:15 ). Your prayers go where you can’t.

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
text: Single Parents, Step-Parents, and Grandparents Single parents. God is a father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows ( Psalm 68:5 ). Timothy knew the holy scriptures from a child, taught by his mother and grandmother. Scripture says only that his father was a Greek ( Acts 16:1 , 2 Timothy 1:5 , 3:15). Ask your church to stand with you, and let godly men and women into your children’s lives. Step-parents. Joseph raised a son who wasn’t his by blood, and Mary still said to Jesus, thy father and I ( Luke 2:48 ). Your authority will grow with trust. At first, let the child’s own parent lead in correction while you win the child’s heart. Never speak against the other parent in his hearing. Grandparents. Children’s children are the crown of old men ( Proverbs 17:6 ). Tell your grandchildren what God has done, as Moses told Israel to teach thy sons, and thy sons’ sons ( Deuteronomy 4:9 ). Pray for them, and stand behind their parents even where you would have done things differently.

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
text: Parenting Under a Patient Father Every honest parent knows how often he has failed. There was the angry word at bedtime, and the promise forgotten. You need more than better methods. You need a Father yourself. Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him. For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust. Psalm 103:13-14 (KJV) God disciplines his children, but always for their good and with great patience. For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness. Hebrews 12:10 (KJV) After their own pleasure means as seemed best to them. Our fathers did what they thought right, and sometimes they got it wrong. God never does ( Hebrews 12:5-11 ). Because he is that kind of Father to you, you can correct your children as he corrects you, patiently and for their good, never to get even. But how does a sinner become one of God’s children? Not by growing up in a Christian home, and not by trying harder. The Son of God bore the wrath that sinners deserved on the cross. On the third day he rose from the dead. All who turn from their sin and trust in him are forgiven and adopted, and receive the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father ( Romans 8:15 ). If you’re not sure you're his, read the gospel and come to him today. Then let your children see grace at work in you. When you sin against them, say so plainly and ask their forgiveness. Few things teach a child the gospel like a parent who repents. Grace never excuses sin, yours or theirs. But it means your home doesn’t have to run on fear. Your children’s deepest need isn’t perfect parents. It’s the Savior their imperfect parents point to.

title: What the Bible Says About Raising Children
section: Begin With What You Can Do Today
text: Begin With What You Can Do Today Begin family worship, or begin again. Tonight after supper, read a short passage, sing a psalm, and pray. Ten minutes is enough. Learn one catechism question together. Say it at meals all week. Spend time alone with each child. With a teenager, ask one real question. Then listen far more than you talk. Look hard at the screens in your home. Start with your own. Settle a rule, explain it, and keep it yourself first. Confess one sin to your children. If you’ve been harsh or absent or unfair, tell them so, and ask their forgiveness. Pray for each child by name every morning. Write down what you ask, so in time you can see what God has done. Ask for help. Talk to your elders, or to an older couple whose children are grown. You were never meant to do this alone.

title: What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline
text: What the rod in Proverbs means, how to correct a child in love and never in anger, and where discipline ends and abuse begins.

title: What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline
section: Why God Commands Parents to Discipline
text: Why God Commands Parents to Discipline God doesn’t leave children to raise themselves. He places them under a father and a mother, and he tells those parents to correct them. That isn’t because God is harsh. It’s because he is a Father himself, and he loves. My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord ; neither be weary of his correction: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth. Proverbs 3:11-12 (KJV) The Lord ’s correction is a mark of his delight. A father who never corrects isn’t kind. He has stopped caring where his child is going. Proverbs says it bluntly. He that spareth his rod hateth his son, but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes ( Proverbs 13:24 ). Betimes means early, while the child is young and the habit is still soft. Hebrews quotes Proverbs 3 to suffering Christians and reasons from the home up to heaven. We gave our earthly fathers reverence when they corrected us, so we should much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live ( Hebrews 12:9 ). For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness. Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby. Hebrews 12:10-11 (KJV) Earthly fathers corrected after their own pleasure, as seemed best to them. They didn’t always get it right. God never errs. Hold the rod with that humility. You're a father under the Father, and you'll give account to him for how you used the authority he lent you. The Larger Catechism sums up what God requires of everyone set over others, parents first of all. to love, pray for, and bless their inferiors; to instruct, counsel, and admonish them; countenancing, commending, and rewarding such as do well; and discountenancing, reproving, and chastising such as do ill Westminster Larger Catechism Q&A 129 Love comes first in that list, and chastising comes near the end. That’s the right order. Correction grows out of love, and it’s only one part of it.

title: What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline
text: The Rod in Proverbs Proverbs speaks of the rod in the correcting of a child in 13:24, 22:15, 23:13-14, and 29:15, and in 29:17 it names the fruit. Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest. Many honest parents aren’t sure how much of this to read literally. Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him. Proverbs 22:15 (KJV) The rod was real The rod in these verses was a real stick, used to strike. Proverbs lays the same rod on the back of a fool ( Proverbs 10:13 , 26:3), and the law of Moses speaks of a master striking a servant with one ( Exodus 21:20 ). It isn’t merely a figure of speech. These proverbs teach that measured physical correction of a child is a right and loving thing. You may not read the rod out of them. The rod also stands for more than itself. The rod and reproof give wisdom ( Proverbs 29:15 ), blows and words together. Foolishness here isn’t childishness. It’s a heart bent on its own way against God and parents. The rod speaks of a parent's responsibility to correct foolishness, while the rest of Scripture governs how that discipline is carried out. But the picture never empties out the thing. The stick was real, and so is the folly. A proverb, not a rulebook Proverbs are sayings of wisdom. They teach a principle and its normal means. They trust the reader to apply them with judgment. Answer not a fool according to his folly, the book says, and in the next verse, Answer a fool according to his folly ( Proverbs 26:4-5 ). Both are true, and wisdom knows which fits the hour. So the rod proverbs don’t tell you what age to begin or end, what instrument to use, or how many strokes. Anyone who hands you a fixed method and calls it God’s is saying more than God said. Nor are the promises machines. Only the Spirit gives a new heart. A child who has been made to behave isn’t yet a child who has been born again. He shall not die Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die. Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell. Proverbs 23:13-14 (KJV) In the English of 1611, beat simply means strike, not what we now call a beating. The verse speaks to a parent who holds back out of soft fear, as though a measured stroke would ruin the child. It won’t, Solomon says. He isn’t drawing the line at death, as if anything short of it were allowed. God’s law limited even a guilty man’s punishment to forty stripes, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee ( Deuteronomy 25:3 ). A master who struck out his servant’s eye or tooth had to set him free ( Exodus 21:26-27 ). If God’s law set bounds for punishing a criminal and a servant, it sets them far more for a little child. Hell in verse 14 is the Hebrew word for the grave and the world of the dead. Folly left alone leads down to death, and many Reformed teachers add, to eternal ruin. Correction is one of God’s means to turn a child from that road. A spanking doesn’t save a soul. Only Christ saves. Where faithful parents differ Godly Reformed parents who believe all of this still differ in practice. Some use a small rod or a wooden spoon, so that the hand stays for comfort. Others use only an open hand. Some spank often while children are very small. Others keep it for open defiance and use it rarely, or stop by six or seven. Some, for a particular child or under a promise they've made, hardly use it at all. These are matters of wisdom, and no parent should bind another’s conscience where Scripture hasn’t. What none may do is call the rod cruel when God calls it love. Nor may anyone make it the whole of raising a child, when God never does.

title: What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline
text: Discipline Is More Than Spanking And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. Ephesians 6:4 (KJV) Nurture is training, and admonition is warning with words. Most discipline in a godly home happens with no rod in sight. Teaching. Talk of God’s ways when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way ( Deuteronomy 6:7 ). Gather them for family worship and teach them the catechism. Warning. Tell the child plainly what is wrong and what will follow, before it happens. A rule he never knew is a trap, not a rule. Consequences. A lost privilege, an early bed, paying for what was broken. These often teach better than a smack. As a child grows they take its place. Example. Children learn more from how you handle your own sin than from how you handle theirs. When you wrong them, ask their forgiveness. Praise. The Catechism counts commending such as do well as part of the duty. Catch your children doing right, and tell them.

title: What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline
text: The Guardrails Scripture Sets The same catechism that requires parents to chastise also names the sins of those in authority. correcting them unduly; careless exposing, or leaving them to wrong, temptation, and danger; provoking them to wrath Westminster Larger Catechism Q&A 130 A parent can sin by never correcting, and a parent can sin by correcting wrongly. Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God. James 1:19-20 (KJV) Never in anger. If you’re angry, wait. Send the child to his room and go pray. A wise man keepeth it in till afterwards ( Proverbs 29:11 ). If you can’t calm down, do not spank today. A stroke in temper only teaches that the bigger person wins. Never to injure. Correction should sting for a moment and then be over. If it leaves a bruise, a welt, or any mark at all, it has gone too far, whatever you meant. Never on the face or the head. Only on the seat. Never shake a child, never use a fist, and never strike anywhere that can be hurt. Mostly for young children. It fits the years before a child can be fully reasoned with. As he grows, words and consequences take over. A spanked teenager is usually shamed rather than corrected. Children differ too. A tender child may need only a word. God knoweth our frame ( Psalm 103:14 ), and you should know your child’s. Private, not humiliating. Never in front of brothers, sisters, or friends, and never with mockery. God would not let even a criminal be made vile in his brother’s eyes ( Deuteronomy 25:3 ). For sin, not for childishness. Spilled milk isn’t rebellion, and a tired toddler isn’t a fool. It is the glory of a man to pass over a transgression ( Proverbs 19:11 ). Keep the rod for willful defiance, and pass over much else. Explained before, and restored after. Tell the child calmly what he did and why it’s wrong. Afterward, hold him, pray with him, and tell him you love him. Then it’s finished, and you don’t bring it up again. Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged ( Colossians 3:21 ). A child corrected too often, too hard, or without warmth doesn’t grow wise. He loses heart. If your children flinch when you come near, stop and examine yourself before God.

title: What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline
text: When Correction Becomes Abuse Abuse isn’t discipline. Striking in rage, leaving bruises, hitting the face or head, shaking a baby, choking, kicking, using a belt or a cord, threatening, terrifying, or shaming a child is a sin against the sixth commandment. That commandment forbids striking and wounding (Larger Catechism Q&A 136). It’s also a crime. To call it biblical discipline is to put God’s name on what God forbids. If you've crossed that line, here is what to do. Stop today. Put the rod away. Don’t take it up again unless your elders, knowing everything, agree. For some parents that will mean never. Tell your pastor. Don’t soften the story. If you’re afraid you will hurt your child, leave the house now. If a child is in danger, call 911 . Let it be reported. Harm to a child must be reported to the police or to child protective services. Don’t ask your child, or anyone in the family, to keep quiet. Accept what the law does, for pardon with God doesn’t cancel earthly justice ( Romans 13:4 ). Get help for your anger. Read My anger frightens my family , and do what it says. Christ turns away no one who comes to him in true repentance. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light ( John 3:21 ), and hiding it isn’t repentance. If you see a child being hurt, in your church or anywhere else, don’t wait for someone else to act. Read If a child is being hurt , and report it. And if you were beaten as a child by someone who said God required it, that wasn’t God’s discipline. He saw it, and he doesn’t ask you to call it love. Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him ( Psalm 103:13 ).

title: What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline
section: What the Law of the Land Says
text: What the Law of the Land Says Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers ( Romans 13:1 ). Know the law where you live. In most of the United States a parent may still use reasonable physical correction. But what counts as reasonable differs by state, and a mark can bring an investigation. Foster parents are almost always forbidden by their license to spank a child placed with them. Many adoption agencies ask the same promise. If you gave it, keep it, as one that sweareth to his own hurt, and changeth not ( Psalm 15:4 ). Many of these children have already been hurt by adults. A stroke may teach them fear rather than wisdom. A number of countries forbid all physical correction of children, Sweden and Scotland among them. If you live under such a law, obey it. Scripture commends the rod as a normal means. But it doesn’t make that one means the only way to keep God’s command to correct your child. Use the others. Don’t decide alone that the law may be broken. Take the question to your elders, for in the multitude of counsellors there is safety ( Proverbs 11:14 ).

title: What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline
text: Discipline Under the Cross But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed. Isaiah 53:5 (KJV) The chastisement of our peace is the punishment that made peace between sinners and God. It fell on Christ. He bore it in full for his people, and he rose on the third day because the debt was paid. Christ bare our sins in his own body on the tree, by whose stripes ye were healed ( 1 Peter 2:24 ). If you don’t yet know him, read The Gospel before anything else on this page. So if you’re in Christ, God’s discipline of you is never payment for your sin. That was paid once, on the cross. The Confession says God’s adopted children are pitied, protected, provided for, and chastened by him as by a father; yet never cast off Westminster Confession of Faith 12.1 A sinning believer may fall under God’s fatherly displeasure ( Westminster Confession 11.5 ), but it’s a Father’s displeasure, not a Judge’s sentence ( Romans 8:1 ). And so you correct your child as one who has been forgiven. You aren’t making him pay for his sin. No child can pay that debt, and only Christ could. You correct to turn him from folly and to point him to the Savior who bore the stripes. When it’s over, tell him of Christ. A parent who remembers how much he has been forgiven won’t correct with contempt. Be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you ( Ephesians 4:32 ).

title: What the Bible Says About Spanking and Discipline
text: Before You Discipline Your Child Settle your own heart first. Read Hebrews 12:5-11 and Psalm 103:8-14 . Ask God to make you toward your children what he is toward you, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy. Agree with your husband or wife. Write a few plain house rules and what follows when each is broken. Then, in a calm hour, explain them to the children. Make a rule for yourself. If you’re angry, you won’t spank. Wait, pray, and come back when you’re calm. Spend time with each child that has nothing to do with correction. Correction lands very differently from a parent who delights in the child. Ask for counsel. Talk with your elders, and with an older couple whose grown children walk with the Lord. If you’ve gone too far, stop and tell your pastor today. See When Correction Becomes Abuse . Pray for their souls by name. Ask God to give each child a new heart. Your rod can restrain folly for a season, but only Christ can make a child his own. The King your children most need to know is the one who shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom ( Isaiah 40:11 ). Correct them in such a way that they can believe it.

title: What the Bible Says About Abortion
text: The unborn child bears the image of God. What Scripture says, the hard cases, help for a mother who is afraid, and mercy for the guilty.

title: What the Bible Says About Abortion
section: What God Says About the Unborn
text: What God Says About the Unborn Every human being bears the image of God. That's why taking an innocent life is so great a wrong. Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man. Genesis 9:6 (KJV) The question of the unborn child's humanity matters because God's command protects innocent human life. Scripture speaks of him that way again and again. For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother’s womb. I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well. Psalm 139:13-14 (KJV) Psalm 139 is poetry. Covered pictures God knitting a body together, and the reins are the inward parts. But the person in the picture is real. David doesn’t say God made some tissue that later became David. He says God covered me. The one praising God in the psalm is the same one who was in the womb. Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Jeremiah 1:5 (KJV) God set Jeremiah apart for his work before he was born. Sanctified here means set apart. God deals with the unborn as persons with names and callings. When Mary came to her cousin Elisabeth, the babe leaped in Elisabeth’s womb for joy ( Luke 1:41 , 44). Luke uses the same Greek word for that unborn John as for the newborn Jesus in the manger ( Luke 2:12 ). He uses it again for the infants brought to Jesus ( Luke 18:15 ). To the Holy Spirit, a baby is a baby, inside the womb or out. Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me. Psalm 51:5 (KJV) David traces his own sin back to his conception. Only a person can be a sinner. So Scripture counts a human being as one of Adam’s fallen race from the very start. The law of Moses guarded the unborn too. If men fought and struck a woman with child, so that her fruit departed, and no harm followed, the man paid a fine. But if harm followed, then thou shalt give life for life ( Exodus 21:22-23 ). The words for her fruit departing are the plain Hebrew words for children going out. That’s how the Bible speaks of birth. Many Reformed teachers read it as a child born early. If mother and child were unharmed, a fine was paid. If either one was harmed or killed, the same justice applied as for any other person. Some read the passage another way, but no reading of it makes the child nothing.

title: What the Bible Says About Abortion
section: The Son of God in the Womb
text: The Son of God in the Womb The strongest word on this is the incarnation itself. The eternal Son of God didn’t come into the world as a grown man. He was conceived. And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS. Luke 1:31 (KJV) The Shorter Catechism says Christ became man by taking to himself a true body and a reasonable soul, being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of the Virgin Mary ( WSC 22 ). From that moment he was God and man in one person. He passed through every stage of life that we pass through, from the womb on, so that he could redeem people at every stage of it. Christ has been a child in the womb. Every unborn child is that small and that hidden, and none of them is beneath his notice.

title: What the Bible Says About Abortion
text: What People Say It is only a clump of cells. So are you, and so am I. From conception the child is a living human being with his own body and his own genetic code, distinct from his mother. He’s growing as fast as he ever will. Size, development, and where he lives don’t decide whether he is human. A newborn is smaller and weaker than a toddler, and no one thinks he matters less. It is my body. The child lives in his mother’s body but isn’t part of it. He often has a different blood type, and half of what he is came from his father. Scripture says something deeper. Ye are not your own, for ye are bought with a price ( 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 ). No one owns his body in a way that gives him the right to end someone else’s life. The child cannot live outside the womb yet. Needing someone to survive doesn’t make anyone less of a person. A newborn can’t live a day without care. Neither can a man on a ventilator. God puts the weak in our care so that we will protect them, not so that we may decide whether they live. It would be cruel to bring a child into poverty or a hard home. A hard life is still a life. The answer to a hard situation is help, not death, and that is where the church is meant to stand ( James 1:27 ). Many children born into hard places have grown up to know Christ. The child will be disabled. And the Lord said unto him, Who hath made man’s mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I the Lord ? ( Exodus 4:11 ). A child with a disability bears God’s image as fully as any other. Jesus said of a man born blind that his blindness was so the works of God should be made manifest in him ( John 9:3 ). Christians should not push their morality on others. Every law pushes someone’s morality on someone. The only question is whose. God gave rulers the sword to punish evil and protect the innocent ( Romans 13:3-4 ). Protecting the weakest people in a land is one of the plainest things a ruler is for.

title: What the Bible Says About Abortion
text: The Hardest Cases These are real, and the people in them deserve patience, not slogans. When a child is conceived by rape. Rape is a monstrous evil, and the woman bears no guilt for it. Under the law of Moses, a man who forced a betrothed woman was put to death, and the woman was counted innocent ( Deuteronomy 22:25-26 ). But the child didn’t commit that crime. The law says every man shall be put to death for his own sin, and not children for their fathers ( Deuteronomy 24:16 ). Ending the child’s life doesn’t undo the first wrong. It adds a second victim. A woman in this place needs her church to surround her and to carry her and her child. She needs them to see that justice is sought against the man. If she can’t raise the child, adoption is a good and loving choice. When the mother’s life is in danger. Sometimes, as in an ectopic pregnancy, a child grows where he can’t survive. If nothing is done, both mother and child will die. Treating the mother to save the one life that can be saved isn't the same as abortion. The aim is to save life, and the child’s death is grieved, not sought. Such cases are rare, and modern medicine can often save both. When you face one, take it to your elders and to a doctor who honors life, and decide it before God with care. When the baby has already died. When a doctor removes a baby who has already died, that's not an abortion. It's care for a mother after a death, and she has nothing to be ashamed of. If that's your sorrow, read If your baby died before birth .

title: What the Bible Says About Abortion
text: If You're Pregnant and Afraid Maybe you didn’t plan this. Maybe you’re young, or alone, or out of money, or someone is telling you this child will ruin everything. The fear is real, and God sees it. Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord : and the fruit of the womb is his reward. Psalm 127:3 (KJV) However this child came, God calls him a gift. He doesn’t give gifts and then walk away from the one who receives them. You don’t have to see the whole road tonight. You only have to keep from the one step that can’t be taken back. Tell someone who will help. Call your pastor or a Christian friend today. If you have no church, call Option Line, 1-800-712-4357 . They answer at any hour and can connect you with a free pregnancy help center near you. Many of those centers give free ultrasounds, baby supplies, and help with housing and work. Do not let anyone rush you. If someone is pressuring you, threatening you, or hurting you, get safe first . No one has the right to force this choice on you. Remember adoption. If you can’t raise this child, there are families waiting and praying for one. Giving your child life and a home is an act of love, not of failure. Pray. Tell God plainly that you’re afraid. Casting all your care upon him, for he careth for you ( 1 Peter 5:7 ).

title: What the Bible Says About Abortion
text: If You've Had an Abortion Maybe it was years ago, and you’ve never told anyone. Maybe you were the father who drove her there, or the parent who insisted, or the one who paid for it. Maybe you worked in a clinic. The guilt you feel isn’t your imagination, and this page won’t tell you it was nothing. A child died. That's why you need a Savior and not just a reassurance. But hear this as clearly as you have ever heard anything. Your sin isn't beyond the blood of Christ. As there is no sin so small but it deserves damnation, so there is no sin so great that it can bring damnation upon those who truly repent. Westminster Confession of Faith 15.4 King David took a man’s wife and then had the man killed. When the prophet showed him his sin, he didn’t excuse it, and God didn’t destroy him. Psalm 51 is the prayer he prayed afterward. Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness. Psalm 51:14 (KJV) Bloodguiltiness is the guilt of having blood on your hands. That's the prayer for you. The apostle Paul once voted for Christians to be put to death ( Acts 26:10 ). He later wrote that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom he counted himself the chief ( 1 Timothy 1:15 ). If Christ saved the chief, he can save you. Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord : though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool. Isaiah 1:18 (KJV) Christ bore the wrath of God for every sin of everyone who trusts in him, this one included. He rose from the dead, and he says, Him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out ( John 6:37 ). Come to him as you are. Confess the sin by name, and don’t dress it up. Then believe what he says, that he is faithful and just to forgive ( 1 John 1:9 ). If you’re already in Christ and this was before you knew him, or even after, it isn’t hanging over you. There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus ( Romans 8:1 ). You may still grieve your child, and you should. Forgiven grief is different from guilty grief. It weeps, but it doesn’t hide from God. Tell your pastor. Many churches have women and men who have walked this same road and found mercy. You were never meant to carry this in secret. If the old guilt keeps coming back after you’ve confessed it, read What I did is too great to forgive .

title: What the Bible Says About Abortion
text: What Christians Should Do The Larger Catechism says the sixth commandment requires all lawful efforts to preserve the life of ourselves and others, and to protect and defend the innocent ( WLC 135 ). Opposing abortion isn’t a hobby for a few believers. It's part of keeping the law of God. Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction. Proverbs 31:8 (KJV) Pray. Pray for mothers in fear, for fathers who have walked away, for the unborn, for clinic workers, and for rulers. Pray that God would turn hearts. Speak the truth. Say plainly that the unborn child is a person and that abortion takes his life. Say it with tears, not contempt, and never without the gospel. Help mothers. Give money, time, diapers, meals, a spare room. Support a pregnancy help center. A church that says no to abortion must say yes to the mother and her child. Consider adoption and foster care. God set the solitary in families ( Psalm 68:6 ). Christians have taken in unwanted children since the earliest days of the church. Vote and call on rulers to protect life. Laws don’t change hearts. But they do restrain evil and protect the weak, which is what God gave them for. Welcome the guilty. There are people in your church who have had abortions. Let them hear from you that Christ forgives, so they never have to wonder whether there is room for them at his table.

title: What the Bible Says About Work
text: God gave work before the fall. Working as to the Lord, a hard boss, laziness and overwork, providing for a family, and resting in Christ.

title: What the Bible Says About Work
section: Work Before the Fall and After It
text: Work Before the Fall and After It Work isn’t part of the curse. God himself worked six days and rested the seventh ( Genesis 2:2 ). Then, before there was any sin in the world, he gave the man a job. And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it. Genesis 2:15 (KJV) This was a real garden, and Adam was to tend it and guard it. To make, keep, and mend things is part of bearing the image of the God who works ( John 5:17 ). Then Adam sinned, and God spoke to him about his work. And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return. Genesis 3:17-19 (KJV) The thorns were real thorns in a real field, but the curse reaches past farming. The creature, meaning the whole creation, was made subject to vanity ( Romans 8:20 ). That’s why the floor you mopped is tracked with mud an hour later and the part you fixed breaks again. It’s why the body that does the work wears out and returns to the ground ( Genesis 3:19 ). The curse didn’t make work evil. It made work hard. Every ache after a long shift points to the One who was made a curse for us ( Galatians 3:13 ).

title: What the Bible Says About Work
section: The Carpenter and Every Lawful Calling
text: The Carpenter and Every Lawful Calling When Jesus taught in the synagogue at Nazareth, his neighbors couldn’t get past what he used to do for a living. Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him. Mark 6:3 (KJV) The eternal Son of God spent most of his years on earth working with his hands. No one wrote down a single job he did, and those years weren’t wasted. When they ended, the Father said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased ( Matthew 3:17 ). And on the night before he died, he took a towel, and girded himself, and washed his disciples’ feet ( John 13:4-5 ). That was a slave’s work. No one who scrubs, hauls, or cleans up after others is doing work beneath the Son of God. Some work is seen and some isn't. Think of those who clean the halls after the building empties, haul out the trash, and fix the broken door before anyone comes. The Lord sees faithful labor even when no one thanks you for it. He is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love ( Hebrews 6:10 ). The psalmist would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of his God than dwell in the tents of wickedness ( Psalm 84:10 ). Keeping a door was humble work, and he counted it an honor. Before the Reformation, many spoke as if priests, monks, and nuns had a calling from God and everyone else merely had jobs. The Reformers taught from Scripture that every lawful calling is service to God. Calvin likened each man’s calling to a post the Lord has set him to keep. He said no task is so lowly that it won’t shine before God when done in obedience to that calling (Institutes 3.10.6). Paul said, Let every man, wherein he is called, therein abide with God ( 1 Corinthians 7:24 ). That doesn’t forbid changing work, for Paul told a slave who could gain his freedom to take it (7:21). It means you serve God where you are. Whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God ( 1 Corinthians 10:31 ). And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men; Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ. Colossians 3:23-24 (KJV) Paul addressed people whose labor was often despised. The janitor, nurse, and parent can likewise serve Christ in daily duties. The Larger Catechism says the eighth commandment requires a lawful calling, and diligence in it ( WLC 141 ). It forbids unlawful callings ( WLC 142 ). Work that's itself sin can’t be done to God’s glory. All other honest work can.

title: What the Bible Says About Work
section: Servants and Masters, Workers and Bosses
text: Servants and Masters, Workers and Bosses Paul wrote to servants and masters in a world full of slavery, and we should be honest about it. Scripture’s words to slaves aren’t approval of man-stealing, which it condemns. God’s law put to death the man who stole a man and sold him ( Exodus 21:16 ), and Paul lists menstealers beside murderers ( 1 Timothy 1:9-10 ). The trade that seized men and women in Africa and sold them in America was man-stealing, and God’s Word stands against it. Most of us aren’t slaves. We agreed to our work, we’re paid for it, and we may leave it. So these words bind us with more force, not less. Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ; Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart; With good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men: Ephesians 6:5-7 (KJV) Eyeservice is working hard only while the boss is watching. Singleness of heart is being the same worker when no one is. A Christian employee does his job as if Christ were his supervisor, because he is. Such faithfulness adorns the doctrine of God our Saviour ( Titus 2:10 ). Bosses aren’t let off. Paul tells masters to do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening, knowing that your Master also is in heaven ( Ephesians 6:9 ). Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven. Colossians 4:1 (KJV) The Larger Catechism places employers under the fifth commandment ( WLC 124 ). They’re to care for those under them, and not seek their own ease and profit at their workers’ cost ( WLC 129-130 ). God’s law told employers to pay the hired man before nightfall ( Deuteronomy 24:15 ), and James warns that wages kept back by fraud cry out to the Lord of sabaoth ( James 5:4 ). When the Boss Is Hard Peter wrote to servants who worked for harsh men. Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward. For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. 1 Peter 2:18-19 (KJV) Froward means crooked and hard to deal with. Peter points you to Christ, who suffered for us, leaving us an example ( 1 Peter 2:21 ). When he was reviled, he reviled not again, and he committed himself to him that judgeth righteously (2:23). He didn’t call the wrong right. He handed it to his Father. So work well under a hard boss, and leave the reckoning to God. But patience isn’t doing wrong when told to. You owe willing obedience to lawful commands ( WLC 127 ). If you're told to lie, cheat, or cover up a crime, answer as the apostles did, We ought to obey God rather than men ( Acts 5:29 ). You may report wrongdoing, seek what you’re owed, and look for other work. If you’re being threatened or hurt, get safe first , and tell your elders.

title: What the Bible Says About Work
section: Diligence, Honesty, and Providing for Your Own
text: Diligence, Honesty, and Providing for Your Own Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: Which having no guide, overseer, or ruler, Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest. Proverbs 6:6-8 (KJV) Solomon means a real ant. No one stands over her, and the work still gets done. The sluggard always means to start after a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands. Then poverty comes on him like an armed man ( Proverbs 6:10-11 ). Paul told the idle in Thessalonica, If any wouldn't work, neither should he eat. He commanded them to work quietly and eat their own bread ( 2 Thessalonians 3:10-12 ). Notice wouldn't. That word is for the unwilling, not the unable. Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth. Ephesians 4:28 (KJV) Thou shalt not steal is also a command to labor (see the commandments in plain words ). The Larger Catechism says it requires truth, faithfulness, and justice in our dealings, and paying back what we have wrongly kept. It forbids fraud, unfaithfulness in matters of trust, and idleness ( WLC 141-142 ). At work that means honest hours, leaving the company’s supplies where they belong, and not calling in sick when you’re well. But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. 1 Timothy 5:8 (KJV) Paul wrote this about caring for widowed mothers, and it reaches every household duty. It doesn’t demand a large wage. It demands what you honestly can. A modest paycheck faithfully earned and brought home is a holy thing.

title: What the Bible Says About Work
text: When Work Becomes an Idol Work can become a god, and so can the money it brings. Jesus said, Ye cannot serve God and mammon ( Matthew 6:24 ). Mammon is wealth, pictured as a master that wants your whole heart. Then Jesus turns straight to anxiety, because worry is one way mammon rules us. Your Father feeds the birds and clothes the lilies, and you’re worth more than they ( Matthew 6:26-30 ). Take therefore no thought for the morrow ( Matthew 6:34 ). It forbids anxious worry, not planning. Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain. It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep. Psalm 127:1-2 (KJV) The psalm doesn’t tell the builders and the watchman to stop working. It tells them the outcome is in God’s hand. The man who works past midnight because everything depends on him is eating the bread of sorrows. Going to bed can be an act of trust. Ecclesiastes sees the worker whose heart taketh not rest in the night, and calls such toil vanity ( Ecclesiastes 2:23 ). Yet it also says a man should make his soul enjoy good in his labour, for that's from the hand of God (2:24). God also built rest into the week. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work ( Exodus 20:9 ), and the seventh is his, for the servant as well as the master. Since Christ rose, that day is the Lord’s Day. Laying your work down for a whole day confesses that God, not your job, holds your life. Read How to Keep the Lord’s Day .

title: What the Bible Says About Work
text: When You Can't Work Maybe you were laid off, or your body has given out, or a disability keeps you from the work others do. Maybe you’re old, and your work has gone to someone younger. It can feel as if you no longer count. Your worth was never in what you produced. You bear God’s image whether you work or not. Paul’s word about the man who won’t work doesn’t touch the man who can’t. For him the church is told to support the weak ( 1 Thessalonians 5:14 ), and Paul worked with his own hands to do just that ( Acts 20:35 ). Receiving that help isn’t shameful. It’s Christ’s body doing what he made it to do. If you’ve lost your job, read My work or my home is gone . If illness has gone on for years, read When it has gone on for years . To the old, God says, Even to hoar hairs will I carry you ( Isaiah 46:4 ). Of the righteous the psalm says, They shall still bring forth fruit in old age ( Psalm 92:12-14 ). The tree is a picture, and the fruit it pictures is real. Prayer, counsel, and telling the next generation of God’s strength ( Psalm 71:18 ) are work too. So is bearing weakness without bitterness. His strength is made perfect in weakness ( 2 Corinthians 12:9 ). If losing your work has made you think others would be better off without you, that thought is a lie. Call 988 or text 988 , and tell someone near you today.

title: What the Bible Says About Work
text: Christ’s Finished Work and Ours The most important thing to say about work is that it can’t save you. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them. Ephesians 2:8-10 (KJV) Christ kept the law we broke, and he bore the curse we earned. On the cross he said, It is finished ( John 19:30 ), and on the third day he rose. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God ( Hebrews 4:9 ). He that's entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his ( Hebrews 4:10 ). The believer has stopped working to be saved. If you’ve been trying to earn God’s favor by being a good worker, stop. Turn from your sin and trust the work Christ finished. If you don’t know him yet, read the gospel . Then you'll work gladly. A saved man doesn’t work to be accepted. He works because he has been accepted, and God receives his weak work for Christ’s sake. Yet notwithstanding, the persons of believers being accepted through Christ, their good works also are accepted in him, not as though they were in this life wholly unblamable and unreprovable in God’s sight; but that he, looking upon them in his Son, is pleased to accept and reward that which is sincere, although accompanied with many weaknesses and imperfections. Westminster Confession of Faith 16.6 That takes in a floor mopped well for Christ’s sake and a meal made for tired children. Your labour is not in vain in the Lord ( 1 Corinthians 15:58 ). Scripture tells us a little of what lies ahead, and we shouldn’t say more than it says. Those who die in the Lord rest from their labours, and their works do follow them ( Revelation 14:13 ). In the city to come there shall be no more curse, and his servants shall serve him ( Revelation 22:3 ). Isaiah speaks of new heavens and a new earth where God’s people shall not labour in vain ( Isaiah 65:17 , 23). Faithful Reformed teachers read that prophecy in more than one way. So hold any picture of work in glory loosely. What is sure is that the curse which made work bitter will be gone.

title: What the Bible Says About Work
section: Faithfulness at Work and at Home
text: Faithfulness at Work and at Home Give your work to God each morning. Pray Moses’ prayer, Establish thou the work of our hands upon us ( Psalm 90:17 ). Do the unseen part well. Pick one thing no one will check, and do it as to the Lord. Set right what is crooked. If you’ve padded hours or taken what wasn’t yours, confess it to God, and pay it back where you can ( WLC 141 ). If you’re over others, check your wages and your words. Pay what is just, and pay it on time. Speak without threats. Honor plain work. Thank the person who cleans your church or your child’s school. Lay the work down on the Lord’s Day. Finish what you can on Saturday, then trust God with what is left. Give from what you earn. Set something aside for the church and for someone in need ( Ephesians 4:28 ). If someone in your church is out of work, tell the deacons and help.

title: What the Bible Says About Money and Debt
text: God owns it all. Contentment, giving, the tithe, borrowing and debt, cosigning, saving, taxes, and help when debt has you under.

title: What the Bible Says About Money and Debt
text: The Earth Is the Lord’s First ask whose money it is. The earth is the Lord ’s, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein. Psalm 24:1 (KJV) God says it again through Haggai, The silver is mine, and the gold is mine ( Haggai 2:8 ). That takes in the paycheck, the truck, and the change in the jar. So we aren’t owners. We're stewards, managing what belongs to another, and one day we’ll give an account. Jesus said, He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much ( Luke 16:10 ). Then he called money the unrighteous mammon, and that which is another man’s (16:11-12). Mammon is money and worldly goods, and it’s lent to us. That’s good news for a family with little. God measures faithfulness by what you do with what’s in the account, not by its size. Forty dollars handled honestly before him isn’t a small thing.

title: What the Bible Says About Money and Debt
section: Contentment and the Love of Money
text: Contentment and the Love of Money But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content. But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition. For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows. 1 Timothy 6:6-10 (KJV) Paul doesn’t say money is the root of all evil. He says the love of it's a root from which every kind of evil grows. They that will be rich means those who want to be. A man can love money with almost none of it. It shows in envy and in the lottery ticket. The snare is a hunter’s trap, and the ruin it pictures is real. Jesus said, Take heed, and beware of covetousness ( Luke 12:15 ). Then he told of a rich man who planned bigger barns and said to his soul, take thine ease. But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee ( Luke 12:19-20 ). The man in the story is made up, but that night is real. It comes for each of us. So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and isn't rich toward God (12:21). Paul knew hunger, and he wrote, I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content ( Philippians 4:11 ). It had to be learned. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me (4:13) was written about that very lesson. Paul spoke of Christ strengthening him to be content in want as well as in plenty. Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee. Hebrews 13:5 (KJV) Conversation means your whole way of life. Contentment rests on God’s promise. Paul also charged the rich to trust not in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy, and to be ready to distribute ( 1 Timothy 6:17-19 ). If you have a warm house and food in the cupboard, don’t be quick to think that charge is only for someone else. The Prosperity Gospel Some preachers teach that God wants every believer rich and healthy, and that enough faith, or a large gift to their ministry, will unlock it.
